body:
B: Hey, Mia, you almost skipped lunch. Do you
know what time it is?
G: Wow, I can’t believe it’s already two. Time flies! I
was so absorbed in working on my new model
airplane. Look! I finished it in just 3 hours.
B: It looks so real. (A)You’re really good at assembling
model airplanes. Did you buy that one?
G: No, I got it from my friend David for my
birthday last week.
B: He definitely knew what you’d love the most.
G: Yes, whenever I work on plastic model airplanes,
I’m totally engaged in assembling them and I
never get distracted.
B: It would be great if you could do what you love
for a living.
G: Yes, that would be nice. But I heard that it’s not
easy to match your career with what you love to
do.
B: It could be difficult, but there are a lot of
people who have become successful by doing
what they love to do.
G: You’re right. I hope I can find such a career.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꾸어 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: You're skilled at assembling model airplanes.
You have a knack for assembling model airplanes.
You can do well at assembling model airplanes.
You have a talent for assembling model airplanes.
You're eager to start assembling model airplanes.
solution: 밑줄 친 (A)의 be good at은 ‘~을 잘하다’라는 뜻으로 누군가 잘하거나 능숙한 것을 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현으로, '너는 모형 비행기를 조립하는 데 정말 능숙하다'라는 뜻이다. 그러나 ❺ ' 너는 모형 비행기 조립을 시작하고 싶어 한다'는 열망을 나타 낼 뿐 능숙함의 의미가 없으므로 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.

body:
I have found that nothing in life is of value (A)[if /
unless] you take risks. Nothing. Now I’m sure in
your experiences in school, in applying to college,
in picking your major, in deciding what you want to
do with life, people have told you to make sure
you have something to “fall back on.” But I never
understood that concept, having something to fall
back on. If I’m going to fall, I don’t want to fall
back on anything. I want to fall forward. This is
what I mean. Reggie Jackson struck out 2,600 times
in his career, the most in the history of baseball.
But you don’t hear about it. People remember the
home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 (B)[failed / successful] experiments because
the 1,001st was the light bulb. Fall forward. Every
failed experiment is one step closer to success.
You’ve got to take risks. I want to talk to you
about why that’s so important. You will fail at some
point in your lives. You will lose. You will embarrass
yourselves. There is no doubt about it. I know
that’s probably not a traditional message for a
graduation ceremony but I’m telling you. Embrace it
because it’s (C)[avoidable / inevitable].

unlessfailedavoidable

body:
Addario’s career took a significant turn when she
went to Afghanistan in 2000. Her photographs
captured the grief, resilience, and courage of
Afghan women. This body of work gained
international ⓐrecognition, serving as a stepping
stone for Addario’s future achievements. Over the
years, Addario’s work has taken her to many
regions torn by war, including Iraq, Sudan, Libya,
and Syria. She knows very well what could happen
in the wars: she was ⓑcaptured twice and was
even threatened with her life. Time and again,
however, she has risked her life to capture images
that speak volumes about the suffering of those
caught in the conflicts between nations.
“The idea of me going to a war zone was out of
the question. Then came 9/11, and it was such a
ⓒdefining moment in history that I felt like I
needed to ⓓcover it. From there I ended up
covering the war in Iraq in 2003 because again, I
felt like I needed to be there. Young soldiers of my
generation were going in to fight, and I thought it
was important to ⓔdocument the war. I’m lucky
because I’ve survived. I’m now at the point in my
life and my career where many of my friends are
not. And so I think it’s important to realize there is
a reason I’m still here, and I have to keep pushing
forward.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 흐름상 영영풀이로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: ⓐ: public attention or approval given for anachievement
ⓑ: to record or represent something in a pictureor other form
ⓒ: very important in shaping what happens afterward
ⓓ: to report on an event or issue for the news
ⓔ: to record information or events as evidence
solution: 지문의 capture는 ‘~을 붙잡다, 포획하다’라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므 로, ‘사진이나 다른 형태로 ~을 기록하거나 나타내다’라는 뜻의 ❷는 문맥상 알맞지 않다.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

We often see individuals who manage to
accomplish seemingly impossible tasks. It almost
appears as if they (A)[lacked / possessed] the ability
to ignite their own spirits. They could be innovators
who achieve success after countless trials and
errors, athletes who push themselves tirelessly until
they go beyond their limits, or activists who are
willing to take risks to (B)[resist / pursue] what they
believe is right. They make us wonder: “What could
be the (C)[driving / restraining] force behind them?
What makes their lives meaningful to them and
even to us?” Let us meet two prominent individuals
and try to answer these questions.
(A)　　　  (B)　　　    (C)
choices: lacked resist   driving
lacked pursue   restraining
possessed resist   restraining
possessed pursue   driving
possessed resist   driving
solution: (A) 앞에서 이들이 ‘겉보기에 불가능해 보이는 일을 성취해 내 는 사람들’이라고 했으므로, 자기 영혼에 불을 붙이는 능력이 ‘부족했다’기보다 그러한 능력을 ‘지니고 있었다’는 흐름이 자 연스러워 possessed(지니고 있었다)가 알맞다. (B) 활동가들이 기꺼이 위험을 감수하는 것은 자신이 옳다고 믿는 바를 이루기 위해 계속 행동하는 모습이므로, resist(저항 하다)보다 pursue(추구하다)가 알맞다. (C) 혁신가는 수많은 시행착오 끝에 성공하고, 운동선수는 자 신의 한계를 넘어설 때까지 쉬지 않고 자신을 밀어붙이며, 활 동가는 위험을 감수하면서도 신념을 실천한다. 이처럼 세 사례 모두 행동을 멈추게 하는 것이 아니라 계속 앞으로 나아가게 하는 힘과 관련되므로, restraining(억제하는)보다 driving(추진 하는, 원동력이 되는)이 알맞다.

body:
In the acting business, you fail all the time. Early
on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact ⓐthat I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just
getting ⓑsmaller and smaller. I didn’t get the job.
But here’s the thing. I didn’t quit. I didn’t fall back.
I walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So
you will catch a break, ⓒwhich is exactly what I
did. Last year I did a play ⓓcalling Fences on
Broadway. It was at the Court Theater. It was at the
same theater ⓔwhich I failed that first audition 30
years prior. The point is every graduate here today
ⓕhave the training and the talent to succeed. But
do you have the courage to fail?

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓓ calling → called ⓔ which → that ⓕ have → has

body:
Researcher and professor Carol Dweck uses the
term mindset to describe the way people think
about ability and talent. Dweck describes two
different mindsets. One is a fixed mindset, which
suggests that your abilities are inherent and
unchangeable. The other is a growth mindset, which
views them as something you can improve through
practice. There are several differences between these
two mindsets. First, in a fixed mindset, you view
failure as permanent, but with a growth mindset,
you see failure as a chance to learn. Second, those
with a fixed mindset are more likely to view
negative feedback as a personal attack, while those
with a growth mindset will see it as a chance to
improve. Lastly, those with a fixed mindset are likely
to give up when they face an obstacle. Meanwhile,
those with a growth mindset will view obstacles as
a chance to experiment and solve problems.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how to overcome failure using a growth mindset
key differences between permanent failure andtemporary failure
how fixed and growth mindsets shape responsesto challenges
the process of measuring a person's inborn abilityand talent
ways to teach children to develop a growth mindset

M: Have you ever heard of the Harvard study that

happy? It’s a revolutionary study in psychology.
It followed the lives of two groups of men for
over 75 years, and it now follows their baby
boomer children to understand how childhood
experience reaches across decades to affect
health and well-being in middle age. So what
keeps us happy and healthy as we go through
life? If you think it’s fame and money, you’re
not alone. But, according to psychiatrist Robert
Waldinger, you’re mistaken.
Waldinger: What keeps us healthy and happy as we
go through life? If you were going to invest, now,
in your future best self, where would you put
your time and your energy? The clearest message
that we get from this 75-year study is this. Good
relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period.

The study explores how childhood experiencesaffect health and well-being in middle age.

I have found that nothing in life is of value unless

experiences in school, in applying to college, in

do with life, people have told you to make sure
you have something to “fall back on.” But I never
understood that concept, having something to fall
back on. If I’m going to fall, I don’t want to fall
back on anything. I want to (A)fall forward. This is
what I mean. Reggie Jackson struck out 2,600 times
in his career, the most in the history of baseball.
But you don’t hear about it. People remember the
home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 failed experiments because the 1,001st was
the light bulb. Fall forward. Every failed experiment
is one step closer to success. You’ve got to take
risks. I want to talk to you about why that’s so
important. You will fail at some point in your lives.
You will lose. You will embarrass yourselves. There

In the acting business, you fail all the time. Early
on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact that I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just

walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So
you will catch a break, which is exactly what I did.
Last year I did a play called Fences on Broadway. It
was at the Court Theater. It was at the same
theater that I failed that first audition 30 years
prior. The point is every graduate here today has
the training and the talent to succeed. But do you
have _____________________________?

the courage to fail
a drive to compete
the ability to avoid failure
the confidence to succeed

“Adapt, stay positive, and learn to do things your
own way.”
Luca “Lazylegz” Patuelli has lived by this motto his
whole life. Born in 1984 with a rare disorder ⓐaffecting
the bones and joints of the body, he has undergone
a total of 16 surgeries since he was 7 months old,
to support his legs, hips, back, and shoulders.
Despite the physical challenges, Lazylegz learned at
an early age about ㉠____________________________. Always
eager to stay active and join his friends in any
activity, he managed to participate in activities such
as soccer, football, and baseball. He also succeeded
in learning how to rock climb and ski, and he
found ways to join his high school swim and dive
teams. As he explored the full range of physical
activities, skateboarding developed into a particular
passion for him.
In 1999, at the age of 15, Lazylegz was introduced
to breakdancing. Immediately, he was attracted to
the music, the culture, and most of all, the
challenging movements. He slowly began creating a
unique style that ⓑmade the most of his upper
body strength. By using his crutches as extensions
of his arms, Bboy Lazylegz was born!
As a professional dancer, he competed and
performed in a wide variety of international dance
events such as Breakin’ Convention, World of Dance,
and Hip Hop International. He created ILL-Abilities
in 2007, an international Bboy crew ⓒcomposed of
some of the world’s best dancers ⓓwho are differently
abled. “We have a message, and that message is
No excuses, no limits. We want to encourage people
of all abilities, all ages, and all races to pursue their
passion, ⓔwhatever it is. Find a way to do it your
own way, and that’s what it is all about.”

body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that companies use to manipulate consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to (A)[stimulate /
prohibit] purchases. This typically comes in three
major forms: insufficient quantities, time, or
availability. We make decisions more quickly under
pressure. The decision is then often made quite
automatically only on the basis of scarcity. After all,
no one wants to miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it easy
for you to see! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost (B)[visible / invisible] in the email. Gray print
on a dark background is rather hard to read, as is
very small print.
Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always
important to be aware that a company’s goals don’t
always (C)[different from / correspond with] your
own. To detect and resist dark patterns, you need
to read carefully and think before you click on a
button.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: stimulate – visible – different from
stimulate – invisible – correspond with
prohibit – invisible – correspond with
prohibit – visible – different from
stimulate – invisible – different from
solution:
1. (A) 수량·시간·이용 가능성을 제한해 압박 속에 빨리 결정하게 만든다는 내용이므로 인위적 희소성은 구매를 ‘자극하기(stimulate)’ 위해 쓰인다.
2. (B) 회색 글씨·아주 작은 글씨처럼 읽기 어렵게 만든다고 했으므로 구독 해지 링크는 거의 ‘보이지 않게(invisible)’ 만들어진다.
3. (C) 앞의 don’t always와 이어져 ‘기업의 목표가 항상 당신의 목표와 일치하지는 않는다’가 되어야 하므로 correspond with가 알맞다(different from은 동사가 아니어서 don’t 뒤에 올 수 없다).
따라서 답은 ②이다.

Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two
artists, mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk
on several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them
to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
㉠______________, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers were being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the (A)[risk / safety] of pedestrians. The idea has
been well received and mirrored in cities of China,
the U.S., Canada, and the UK as well.
㉡______________, traffic engineers design pavement
markings on the roads that drive people to change
their behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one
of the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea.
In 2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion that they are
(B)[speeding up / slowing down], which prompts
them to step on the brakes. Chicago traffic
engineers reported a 36% (C)[surge / reduction] in
crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive curve in the
first six months after painting the lines. Since then,
the Chicago Department of Transportation has
painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

(B) 위험한 커브길의 앞의 도로의 일련이 선 간격이 점점 좁아 지게 되어 있고, 이는 운전자들이 브레이크를 밟도록 유도한다 고 언급되었으므로 운전자들이 ’속도를 내고 있다는(speeding up)‘ 착각을 준다는 흐름이 알맞다. (C) 시카고의 교통부는 이후에도 유사한 커브길에 간격을 둔 선들을 그렸으므로 이 선들이 안전에 효과가 있었다는 것을 알 수 있다. 따라서 교통 공학 전문가들은 이 선을 그린 후 6 개월 동안 커브길에서 추돌 사고가 36% ’감소(reduction)'했다 는 흐름이 알맞다.

You have probably received a notification from
your smartphone telling you that it is time to
exercise or move. These devices lead people to
move by sending notifications when they have been
(A)[active / inactive] for a set amount of time. You
may not have realized it, but this is an example of
a nudge.
A nudge is an intervention that gently guides
individuals toward a desired action, without
forbidding any options. For example, if a school
wants to reduce the amount of sugary drinks that
students consume, then making them less (B)[visible
/ invisible] than bottled water counts as a nudge,
while banning them altogether does not.
Having been studied in the domain of behavioral
economics and marketing, nudging can be applied
to inducing people to make better or ideal
decisions. Here are some ways nudges have
succeeded in bringing about positive changes by
(C)[tweaking / maintaining] people’s choices.

(B) 너지는 어떤 선택지도 금지하지 않으면서 원하는 행동으로 개인을 부드럽게 안내하는 개입이므로, 그 예시로 학교에서 단 음료의 양을 줄이기 위해서는 생수보다 덜 ’눈에 띄게(visible)‘ 배치하는 것이 흐름상 자연스럽다. body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that companies use to manipulate consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark pattern
where your credit card is automatically charged as
soon as a free trial comes to an end. While the
companies that do this would argue that it enables
users (A)[continuing / to continue] to access their
service uninterrupted, users receive no warning that
their cards are about to be charged, often causing
them to be billed unexpectedly. This method is
used by many streaming platforms, but it is also
common with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it
(B)[easy / easily] for you to see! So the
“unsubscribe” link is made almost invisible in the
email. Gray print on a dark background is rather
hard to read, as (C)[is / are] very small print.
Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always
important to be aware that a company’s goals don’t
always correspond with your own. To detect and
resist dark patterns, you need to read carefully and
think before you click on a button.

move by sending notifications when they have been
inactive for a set amount of time. You may not

individuals toward a desired action, without
forbidding any options. For example, if a school
wants to reduce the amount of sugary drinks that
students consume, then making them less visible
than bottled water counts as a nudge, while
banning them altogether does not.

to inducing people to make better or ideal
decisions. Here are some ways nudges have

tweaking people’s choices.

Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two artists,
mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on
several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, ⓐcausing
them to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers ⓑwere being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the safety of pedestrians. The idea has been well
received and ⓒmirrored in cities of China, the U.S.,
Canada, and the UK as well.
Likewise, traffic engineers design pavement markings
on the roads that drive people ⓓto change their
behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one of
the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea. In
2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion ⓔwhich they are
speeding up, which prompts them to step on the

Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that companies use to manipulate consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.

다는 뜻은 아니다! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost invisible in the email. Gray print on a dark
background is rather hard to read, as is very small
print. Dark patterns are everywhere. It is always

resist dark patterns, you need to read carefully and
think before you click on a button.

solution: ㉠ 첫 번째 문단은 많은 사람들이 대다수의 행동에 자신의 행 동을 맞추도록 영향을 주는 표지판 글에 대해 설명하고 있으 나, 뒤에 이어지는 두 번째 문단은 에너지 절약에 있어 남에게 맞추는 것이 더 큰 소비량으로 이어져 너지가 반드시 계획대 로 되지 않는 상황을 언급하고 있으므로 앞 뒤 반대되는 내용 을 이끄는 ‘However(그러나)’ 또는 ‘Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구 하고)’가 들어가는 것이 알맞다. ㉡ 너지로 사람들이 좋은 선택을 하도록 만드는 것이 반드시 계획대로 되지 않는다는 앞 문장에 이어 주민들에게 이웃들의 평균 에너지 사용량에 대한 정보를 제공했을 때, 예상과 달리 에너지 소비가 낮은 가정의 소비량이 더 늘었다는 예시가 이 어지고 있으므로, ‘예를 들어’의 의미를 갖는 For instance 또는 For example이 알맞다.

“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”
“Zambezi?”
“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”
So the elephant was alive! Aaron beamed, his heart beating faster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, ⓐwas covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble breathing. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, flashed through Aaron’s mind, and he felt a lump in his throat.
Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, ⓑreached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly warm. Zambezi opened one eye. Slowly, his trunk curled upward and brushed Aaron’s arm.
“How are you?” Aaron whispered.
He sat down on the straw, and the elephant rested his trunk on Aaron’s leg. They stayed like that for some time, while Samuel watched them ⓒcuriously.
“Here,” Samuel whispered, handing a milk bottle to Aaron. “Maybe you will have better luck than we’ve had.”
Aaron had seen enough babies nurse ⓓto know what to do. He tilted the bottle, spilling some drops onto the elephant’s lip. Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle, looking Aaron in the eyes as he ⓔdid. Samuel shook his head in amazement. Aaron’s mind rushed back to the day he first met the elephant.

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, ⓐby which he has been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. ⓑWith the cook and the gardener pull from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

What was the baby elephant doing in the swimming pool?
What were the staff members gathered by the pool doing before Aaron returned?
Who else jumped into the pool to assist Aaron in rescuing the elephant?
According to the men’s conversation, what had happened to the mother elephant?
solution:

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I ⓐdo. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart ⓑhammering in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi ⓒswallowed pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. (A) He felt ⓓproud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel. (B) Each time he saw the veterinarian ⓔfrown, Aaron’s stomach got tense. (C) When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. (D) One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow ⓕcomparing to his own. (E) Samuel reassured him that all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But that didn’t stop Aaron from worrying. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well ⓖwhat medicine couldn’t cure everything.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 알맞은 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ 동사(sat)가 있는 완전한 절(Aaron sat straight up)에 접속사 없이 다른 절이나, 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으며, 흐름상 주절의 주어와 다른 의미상의 주어 heart가 남아있으며 부대상황(~하면서)을 나타내는 독립분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 의미상 주어 heart가 그의 가슴에서 심장이 ‘쿵쾅거리는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 hammering은 알맞다.
ⓓ 2형식 동사 felt의 보어 자리로 형용사 proud는 알맞다.
ⓔ 과거동사 saw와 목적어 the veterinarian에 이어져 ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형, 능동·진행일 때는 현재분사, 수동일 때는 과거분사가 쓰인다. 목적어 the veterinarian이 ‘얼굴을 찌푸리는’ 주체이므로, 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 frown은 알맞다.
오답
ⓐ do → am (‘~도 (마찬가지로) 그러하다’의 뜻으로 쓰인 부사절 접속사 as가 이끄는 절에서 주어에 이어지는 동사 자리로, 흐름상 앞의 be동사가 쓰인 be proud를 대신해야 하므로, do를 주어에 일치시킨 현재시제 am으로 고친다.)
ⓒ swallowed → to swallow (to부정사 to get과 Bezi에 이어져 ‘get+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하도록 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 to부정사를 쓰므로 swallowed를 to swallow로 고친다.
ⓕ comparing → compared (완전한 절(Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow)에 이어지는 분사 자리로 앞 문장 Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow을 부연 설명하고, 앞 문장이 ‘비교되는’ 대상이므로 comparing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 compared로 고친다.)
ⓖ what → that (완전한 절(medicine couldn’t cure everything)을 이끌어 동사 knew의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)

One morning, Aaron watched sadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the ⓐcompany of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to where Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck lay the ⓑstill, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian ⓒcovered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine.
It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall that Aaron realized with a start that he’d ⓓremembered all about Zambezi. He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable.
He had been preparing himself for the ⓔworst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.
윗글을 다음과 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
After tending to a newly injured elephant, Aaron realized that he had inadvertently (A)______ Bezi and hurried back to him, only to find the little elephant showing signs of (B)______.
(A) (B)
choices: nursed deterioration
attended anxiety
neglected recovery
disregarded decline
overprotected improvement
solution:
[요약문] 새로 다친 코끼리를 돌본 후, Aaron은 자신도 모르게 Bezi를 (A)소홀히 했다는 것을 깨닫고 서둘러 그에게 돌아갔지만, 어린 코끼리가 (B)회복의 징후를 보이고 있는 것을 발견했다.

① 돌본 악화

Bezi was (A)______. His sunken skin slowly gave way to a round belly, and his cheeks filled out, too. Before long, he was moving around more, even trying to leave his stall. The other orphans approached curiously, prodding him all over with their trunks.
Eventually, Bezi was allowed to venture outside. He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk.
(B)Aaron은 여전히 자신을 필요로 하는 아기 코끼리 가까이에서 잠을 자며, 밤낮으로 지켜보고 그 또는 그녀에게 먹이를 준다. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.
윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: getting better each day
losing interest in his daily activities
showing little interest in his surroundings
remaining dependent on human attention
becoming increasingly restless inside his stall
solution:
Bezi의 움푹 들어간 피부가 둥근 배로 바뀌고 볼에도 살이 차올랐으며, 움직임이 활발해지고 다른 코끼리들과 어울리며 바깥으로 나가 진흙에서 즐겁게 첨벙거릴 때 그의 눈은 빛이 났다고 설명하고 있으므로, Bezi가 활기를 찾고 건강을 회복하고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ① ‘날마다 더 좋아지고 있는’이 알맞다.

② 그의 일상 활동에 흥미를 잃어 가고 있는
③ 그의 주변 환경에 거의 관심을 보이지 않는
④ 인간의 관심에 계속 의존한 채 남아있는
⑤ 그의 우리 안에서 점점 더 안절부절못하고 있는

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and it seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering in his chest. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts that Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The head keeper was aware that Aaron had saved Bezi from the pool.
Aaron’s mother said that his father would be proud of him for working at the orphanage.
Aaron barely slept, jolting upright whenever Bezi let out a snort.
Aaron missed his sister’s breathing but gradually found comfort in Bezi and the scent of straw.
Bezi took his medication on his own and gradually recovered, spending less and less time in the stable.
solution:
Samuel과 사육사들은 Aaron에게 Bezi이 약을 먹도록 하는 속임수를 보여주었고, Bezi는 여전히 아파 대부분의 시간을 마구간에서 잠으로 보냈다고 언급하고 있으므로, ⑤ ‘Bezi는 스스로 약을 먹었고 점차 회복하여 마구간에서 보내는 시간이 점점 줄어들었다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 수석 사육사는 Aaron이 수영장에서 Bezi를 구했다는 것을 알고 있었다.
② Aaron의 어머니는 그가 고아원에서 일하는 것에 대해 그의 아버지가 그를 자랑스러워하실 것이라고 말했다.
③ Aaron은 Bezi가 코를 힝힝거릴 때마다 놀라 벌떡 일어나면서 거의 잠을 자지 못했다.
④ Aaron은 그의 여동생의 숨소리를 그리워했지만, 점차 Bezi와 짚 냄새에서 위안을 찾았다.

body:
The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage (A)[by which / in which] the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, ⓐ______. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, (B)[shook / shaking]. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them (C)[waving / to wave] their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: by which shook waving
in which shaking to wave
in which shook waving
by which shaking to wave
in which shaking waving
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(he had been working for a few months)을 이끌고, 선행사인 장소 명사구 Lion’s Inn을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 흐름상 ‘work in ~(~에서 일하다)’의 전치사 in을 사용한 ‘전치사+관계대명사’인 in which가 적절하다.
본문변형 where → in which
(B) (동사(watched)가 있는 완전한 절(He watched the elephant)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 the elephant를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상의 주어인 the elephant가 ‘몸을 떠는’ 주체이고 동사 shake는 ‘떨다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰였으므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 shaking이 적절하다.
(C) ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(…가 ~하는 것을 보다)’의 5형식 구문에서 지각동사 see의 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형이나 현재분사를 사용하며, 목적어 them(some men in uniform)이 ‘흔드는’ 주체이고 목적어 their arms가 이어지므로 능동이자 진행 중인 동작을 나타내기 위해 쓰인 현재분사 waving이 적절하다.

body:
W: Take a look outside your window. Is it hot and sunny? Is it cloudy and rainy? Is there snow on the ground? When you look out the window, you’re seeing what the weather is like today. Weather is only temporary. For example, a heavy snow can turn into a flood after just a few warm spring days. Climate, on the other hand, is more than just a few warm or cool days. Climate describes the typical weather conditions in an entire region for a very long time, 30 years or more. Keeping an eye on changing weather can help us plan ahead. We know if black clouds are forming overhead, it’s probably a good idea to stay inside. But it’s important to keep an eye on changes in the earth’s climate, too.

다음 담화의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Weather tells us about temporary conditions, whereas climate shows the typical patterns of a region over a much longer period.
Since climate varies from region to region, we need to understand the climate characteristics of each region.
Weather patterns in a region can be predicted accurately by observing short-term changes in temperature.
Climate change occurs so slowly that it has very little impact on our daily lives.
We should take action to prevent global warming and extreme weather disasters.
solution: 창밖의 기온, 구름, 비, 눈 등을 통해 확인할 수 있는 날씨는 며칠 사이에도 달라질 수 있는 일시적인 현상인 반면, 기후는 30년 이상의 오랜 기간에 걸쳐 한 지역에서 전형적으로 나타나는 날씨 조건을 의미한다고 설명하므로 이 담화의 요지로 ❶ ‘날씨는 우리에게 일시적인 상태에 대해 알려 주는 반면, 기후는 훨씬 더 긴 기간에 걸친 한 지역의 전형적인 패턴을 보여 준다.’가 적절하다.

body:
Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people (A)[to track / track], adapt to, and even control the weather. Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer (B)[that / what] could measure temperature. The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. The weather — or more broadly, the climate — (C)[has caused / causing] significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: to track / that / causing
track / what / has caused
to track / that / has caused
track / that / has caused
to track / what / causing
solution:
(A) 현재완료형 동사 have allowed의 목적격보어 자리로, allow는 5형식 구문(allow+목적어+목적격보어)으로 쓰일 때 to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하는 동사이므로, 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 to부정사 to track이 알맞다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(could ~ temperature)을 이끌어 명사구 a thermometer를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 알맞다.
(C) 주어 The weather와 대시(—)로 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 ‘or more broadly, the climate’에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로 has caused가 알맞으며 과거부터 현재까지 인류 역사 전반에 걸쳐 중대한 사건들을 초래해 왔음을 나타내고 있다.

body:
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard ⓐto say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that ⓑremain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we ⓒwill be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears ⓓto be as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it ⓔlook like an enormous snowball.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ will be → would be
ⓓ to be → to have been

There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered ⓐthat humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed ⓑto evolve in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally ⓒinterrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period ⓓthat occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it ⓔhad not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓑ to evolve → to have evolved (‘be believed+to부정사‘는 '…가 ~라고 믿어진다[여겨진다]’의 의미로, 호모 사피엔스가 진화한(evolve) 것은 그것이 여겨지는 현재 시점(is believed)보다 더 먼저 일어난 일이므로 앞선 시점을 나타내는 완료 부정사 to have p.p.를 써야 한다. 따라서 to evolve를 to have evolved로 고친다.)

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how desperate things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

(A) At the height of their civilization, the Mayans achieved remarkable milestones in architecture, astronomy, and mathematics. (T/F)
(B) The practice of clearing and burning forests for farming helped reduce severe deforestation across the Yucatán Peninsula. (T/F)
(C) The Yucatán Peninsula mainly relied on rainfall for water, so underground root systems were essential to preserving its water resources. (T/F)
(D) Over a two-century span, researchers discovered that annual rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula was reduced to 70 percent of its previous level. (T/F)
(E) The collapse of the Mayan civilization appears to have been sparked by severe droughts alongside wars and other conflicts. (T/F)

다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
choices: T-F-T-T-F
T-F-T-F-T
F-F-T-F-T
T-F-F-F-T
F-T-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-F-T이다.
(A) 자신들의 문명이 절정에 달했을 때, 마야인들은 건축, 천문학, 수학에서 놀라운 성과를 이루었다. (일치)
at the height of ~ ~이 절정에 있는[달했을 때]
(B) 농사를 짓기 위해 숲을 개간하고 불태우는 관행은 유카탄반도 전역의 심각한 삼림 벌채를 줄이는 데 도움이 되었다(→가져왔다). (불일치)
(C) 유카탄반도는 주로 강수에 수자원을 의존했으며, 지하 근계는 이 지역의 수자원을 보존하는 데 필수적이었다. (일치)
(D) 2세기에 걸친 기간 동안, 연구자들은 유카탄반도의 연간 강수량이 이전 수준의 70퍼센트로(→70%만큼이나) 감소했다는 것을 발견했다. (불일치)
(E) 마야 문명의 붕괴는 전쟁 및 다른 갈등과 함께 심각한 가뭄에 의해 촉발된 것으로 보인다. (일치)

One of the most famous pieces of art in the world may have been inspired by an unusual weather event. A study suggests that the sky (A)[was depicted / depicted] in Edvard Munch’s The Scream may actually be an accurate representation of a weather phenomenon known as “Mother of Pearl Clouds,” a rare phenomenon (B)[what / that] may have a big impact on anyone who sees it for the first time. The typical colors in this rare weather event are the same as the colors in Munch’s painting, and the circumstances under which these rare clouds form (C)[match / to match] Munch’s environment at the time he conceived The Scream.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

choices: depicted / that / to match
was depicted / what / match
depicted / what / to match
depicted / that / match
was depicted / that / match
solution:
(A) 뒤에 조동사 may가 이어지므로 that절의 주어 the sky를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, the sky가 ‘그려진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 depicted가 적절하다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(may ~ time)을 이끌어 명사구 a rare phenomenon을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
(C) 관계사절(under which ~ form)의 수식을 받는 주어 the circumstances에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로 match가 적절하다.

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways to influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
There have been two main approaches aimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere more reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it reaches the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would be fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or breaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials. (A)______, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to fertilize ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while taking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ emitted into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and isolate CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. (B)______, some believe that we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: In addition / In fact
For instance / In other words
Moreover / Nevertheless
For example / Still
Therefore / That is
solution:
(A) 앞에서 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하여 지하에 저장하거나 안정적인 물질에 탄소를 가두는 접근법을 설명하고, 뒤에서는 철가루를 바다에 뿌려 식물성 플랑크톤의 성장을 촉진함으로써 대기 중 이산화탄소를 줄이는 구체적인 방법을 제시하므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 For instance(예를 들어), For example(예를 들어)가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에서 탄소 포집 기술이 전 세계 배출량을 기껏해야 10%까지 줄이는 데 그칠 수 있다는 한계를 제시한 뒤, 뒤에서 이러한 한계에도 불구하고 기후 변화를 늦추기 위해 여러 해결책을 함께 추진해야 한다는 견해를 언급하므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고), Still(그럼에도 불구하고)이 적절하다.

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists ______, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

look away from the realities of the world

seek refuge in ideal and untouched natural landscapes
solution: 산업혁명 시기에 대기 오염이 심해지면서 인상주의 화가 Turner와 Monet의 그림 속 하늘도 점점 더 흐려졌다는 것을 밝혀냈다는 한 연구 결과에 이어, Turner와 Monet 같은 인상주의 화가들은 당시의 대기 변화를 ‘더’ 예민하게 파악했을 것이라는 내용이 and로 이어지고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 많은 화가들도 동일하게 주변 환경의 변화를 파악하고 그림에 반영했을 것이라는 내용이 들어가야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ❹ ‘주위 환경의 변화로부터 영감을 얻다’가 적절하다.

Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.

Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. (A) But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. (B)
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. (C) During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle. (D)
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. (E) When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?

body:
Fog (A)[Saves / Dooms] the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally (B)[detected / undetected] by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in (C)[defeat / victory] for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Saves / detected / victory
Dooms / detected / defeat
Saves / undetected / victory
Saves / undetected / defeat
solution:

(B) 혁명군이 안개 덕분에 몇백 미터 떨어진 곳의 영국군에게 발각되지 않은 채 이스트강을 건넜다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 undetected(발각되지 않은)가 적절하다.
(C) 뒤에서 미국을 독립적인 국가로 만들었다고 했으므로 미국 혁명이 신생 식민지들의 승리로 끝났다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 victory(승리)가 적절하다.

When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. (A)Aaron은 Lion 여관으로 향했고, 그곳에서 그는 몇 개월 동안 일해 오고 있었다. One of the boys ⓔwho worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, ⓕlain on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.

One morning, Aaron watched sadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the company of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to where Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck lay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. (A) He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine. (B) He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable. (C) He had been preparing himself for the worst, but ⓐhe got a shock of a different kind. (D) The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. (E) He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant (A)______. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together ⓐthey were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. With the cook and the gardener pulling from the edge, Aaron and the other boy finally managed to drag, pull, and push the exhausted animal onto the deck. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw ⓑthem waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old … found the mother … killed … poachers ….” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

swam calmly toward the edge
waved its trunk at the workers

body:
When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”

“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”

On a dusty truck lay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from ⓒcatching in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets to cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine.
It wasn’t until the new elephant was settled in her stall ⓓwhich Aaron realized with a start that he’d forgotten all about Zambezi. He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable.
He ⓔhad been preparing himself for the worst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk hanging over the half wall of his stall. He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.

Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk.
(D)Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. (E)Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: Bezi는 날마다 더 좋아져 더 많이 움직이고 바깥으로 나가 다른 고아 코끼리들을 따라다니며 그들의 행동을 흉내 내고, Aaron은 여전히 자신을 필요로 하는 아기 코끼리들을 밤낮으로 돌보면서 모든 고아 코끼리들이 자유로운 야생 동물로 아프리카 평원을 돌아다닐 날을 꿈꾼다고 설명하고 있으므로, 다른 동물들의 행동을 모방하는 것의 단점을 언급한 (C) ‘다른 동물들의 행동을 모방하는 것은 때때로 어린 동물들이 낯선 상황에 대처하는 독자적인 방식을 발달시키는 것을 방해할 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
Aaron awoke from his thoughts when the head keeper found him and Samuel and said, “So, you are the boy who rescued Bezi from the pool. How would you like to work here? We’re short on workers, and ⓐit seems you’re good with animals.”
When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
The first few nights at the orphanage ⓑwas not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, (A)______. He missed the familiar sounds and smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw.
Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check. Bezi was still very sick, ⓒwas slept most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours.
Aaron recorded the amounts ⓓthat Bezi drank. He held Bezi’s head as the veterinarian took his temperature or administered medicine. He even recorded the elephant’s bowel movements. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
But mothers worry, and so did Aaron. Each time he saw the veterinarian ⓔfrowns, Aaron’s stomach got tense. When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow compared to his own. Samuel reassured him ⓕwhom all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But that didn’t stop Aaron from worrying. Bezi still had a fever. Aaron knew only too well that medicine couldn’t cure everything.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ, ⓕ이다.
ⓑ was → were (주절의 주어 The first few nights at the orphanage의 핵심 단어인 복수명사구 The first few nights에 수일치해야 하므로, was를 복수동사 were로 고친다.)
ⓒ was slept → sleeping (동사(was)가 있는 완전한 절(Bezi was still very sick)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 Bezi를 부연 설명하는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 분사구문의 의미상의 주어인 Bezi가 ‘잠을 자는’ 주체이므로 was sleeping을 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 sleeping으로 고친다.)
ⓔ frowns → frown 또는 frowning (과거동사 saw와 목적어 the veterinarian에 이어져 ‘see+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 듣다)’의 지각동사의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리로, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동일 때는 동사원형, 능동·진행일 때는 현재분사, 수동일 때는 과거분사가 쓰인다. 목적어 the veterinarian이 ‘얼굴을 찌푸리는’ 주체이므로, frowns를 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 frown 또는 능동·진행의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 frowning으로 고친다.)
*원래 지문에는 frown이 쓰였음
ⓕ whom → that (완전한 절(all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans)을 이끌어 동사 reassured의 목적격 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, whom을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ It seems (that) ~(~인 것 같다)의 문장 구조로, 완전한 절(you’re good with animals)을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that이 생략되었고, 앞의 형식주어 it은 알맞다.

When Aaron arrived at the orphanage, two men were playing a board game with bottle caps at the gate. One of the men recognized him and called out, “Good afternoon, Aaron!”
“Hello,” Aaron answered shyly.
“I’m Samuel. Did you come to visit Zambezi?”
“Zambezi?”
“It’s the name we gave the little elephant.”
So the elephant was alive! Aaron beamed, his heart ⓐbeaten faster. Samuel motioned for him to follow. Zambezi lay on a bed of straw in a corner of a stall. He looked like a wrinkled bag of bones, covered by blankets. He seemed to be having trouble breathing. The image of his father, lying under blankets at home just before he died, ⓑflashing through Aaron’s mind, and he felt a lump in his throat.
Samuel nudged him forward. Aaron knelt and, with shaking hands, reached out to touch Zambezi’s thick skin. It felt surprisingly ⓒwarmly. Zambezi opened one eye. Slowly, his trunk curled upward and brushed Aaron’s arm.
“How are you?” Aaron whispered.
He sat down on the straw, and the elephant rested his trunk on Aaron’s leg. They stayed like that for some time, while Samuel watched them curiously.
“Here,” Samuel whispered, handing a milk bottle to Aaron. “Maybe you will have better luck than we’ve had.”
Aaron had seen enough babies nurse to know what to do. He tilted the bottle, spilling some drops onto the elephant’s lip. Zambezi licked the milk off his lip and then began to suck from the bottle, looking Aaron in the eyes as he ⓓwas. Samuel shook his head in amazement. Aaron’s mind rushed back to the day ⓔwhich he first met the elephant.

He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
(C) The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. But it wasn’t long before he began to find comfort in the closeness of Bezi and the warm smell of straw. Samuel and the other keepers showed him tricks to get Bezi to swallow pills and how to take blood for the veterinarian to check.

choices: that didn’t stop Aaron from worrying

When Aaron went back home and told his mother about the job, she said, “Your father would be proud, as I am. We’ll miss you, but we’ll manage. And, of course, you’ll come home on your days off.” And just like that, his decision was made.
(A) But mothers worry, and so did Aaron. Each time he saw the veterinarian frown, Aaron’s stomach got tense. When Bezi spat out his medicine, Aaron feared that he’d never get better. One morning, he noticed that Bezi’s heartbeat was very, very slow compared to his own. Samuel reassured him that all elephants have a slower heartbeat than humans. But ⓐ______. (B) Bezi was still very sick, sleeping most of the day in the quiet stable. But now, at least, he drank the bottles that the keepers offered him every few hours. He felt proud when Bezi finished his milk and covered him with a blanket at night. “I’m turning into an elephant mother,” he joked to Samuel.
(C) The first few nights at the orphanage were not easy. Aaron hardly slept at all. With every snort Bezi gave, Aaron sat straight up, heart hammering smells of home, especially his sister’s soft, rhythmic breathing as she slept near him. The veterinarian’s expression and Bezi‘s spitting out his medicine made Aaron fear that Bezi would not recover.

Aaron wasn't startled awake by the sound of Bezi’s snoring because he missed the familiar sounds. was familiar with that sound.
solution:

One morning, Aaron watched sadly as the other elephants played, kicking a large can and rolling joyfully in the mud. He was wishing Bezi could have the company of other elephants, when suddenly he heard Samuel shout, “Come quick!” Aaron dropped the rake he was holding and ran to ⓐwhich Samuel and the other keepers crowded. On a dusty truck ⓑlay the still, gray body of a young elephant. She had an ugly wound on one of her feet from being caught in a trap.
After eight men carried her to a stall in the stable, the veterinarian covered her leg with green clay, a natural healing remedy. Aaron ran for blankets ⓒto cover the injured elephant. He stroked her head while the veterinarian checked her heart rate and administered medicine.
(A)새 코끼리가 자신의 우리에 적응하고 나서야 Aaron은 깜짝 놀라며 자신이 Zambezi에 대한 모든 것을 잊고 있었다는 것을 깨달았다. He had never left him alone this long before. He couldn’t believe he’d been so careless! What if something had happened to him? Aaron dashed toward the stable.
He had been preparing ⓓhimself for the worst, but he got a shock of a different kind. The little elephant was standing up with his trunk ⓔto hang over the half wall of his stall. He seemed to be trying to reach some plastic bottles. Aaron laughed with relief. “Bezi! Are you hungry? Are you getting into trouble now? I guess that’s a good sign!” He rubbed the little elephant’s trunk, and Bezi nuzzled Aaron’s arm.

The sun was a glowing red ball in the eastern sky when Aaron left his family’s hut. Aaron headed to Lion’s Inn, where he had been working for a few months. As Aaron approached the gate, he was startled by a strange noise. He couldn’t believe his eyes — a small elephant was flailing around in the swimming pool! The elephant held its trunk in the air and kicked wildly.
Aaron glanced around nervously for the mother elephant. But there were no other elephants in sight, and this one needed help fast. Aaron raced to the cottage where the gardener slept. “Help! Hurry!” he called. He ran to the pool shed and grabbed a rope and a rake. When he got back, the manager, the gardener, the cook, and other workers had gathered by the pool.
After Aaron threw the rake down on the deck, he jumped straight into the water. The little elephant snorted and splashed wildly. Aaron got close to it with the rope. One of the boys who worked in the kitchen jumped in, too. Together they were able to get the rope under the elephant’s belly. (A)요리사와 정원사가 가장자리에서 잡아당기고, Aaron과 다른 소년은 그 기진맥진한 동물을 끌고, 당기고, 밀어서 간신히 덱 위로 올려놓았다. He watched the elephant, lying on its side, shaking. It looked straight at Aaron and blinked.
A truck pulled up, and some men in uniform stepped out. Aaron saw them waving their arms and overheard bits and pieces of their conversation with the inn manager: “only one month old ... found the mother ... killed ... poachers ....” The men loaded the elephant into the truck.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Aaron was astonished to see a little elephant struggling in the pool, raising its trunk into the air and kicking violently.
Aaron anxiously glanced around in search of the mother elephant, but there was no sign of any other elephants.
While Aaron called for help and fetched the rescue tools, the manager and other staff gathered beside the pool.
Aaron got out of the pool and stood aside, waiting for the other keepers to save the young elephant.
Several uniformed men got out of the truck and loaded the month-old elephant whose mother had been killed by poachers.
solution:
Aaron은 갈퀴를 덱 위로 던지고 물속으로 뛰어들어 밧줄을 들고 코끼리에게 다가갔으며, 부엌에서 일하던 소년 한 명도 구조를 위해 물에 뛰어들었다고 언급하고 있으므로, ❹ ‘Aaron은 수영장 밖으로 나와 옆에 서서 다른 사육사들이 그 어린 코끼리를 구해 주기를 기다렸다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답

③ Aaron이 도움을 요청하고 구조 도구들을 가져오는 동안, 관리자와 다른 직원들은 수영장 옆에 모였다.

Eventually, Bezi ______. He seemed to love the older orphans, following them around the pen and imitating their behavior. Bezi’s eyes lit up as he splashed in the mud. And whenever he spotted Aaron, he came running over to search for a bottle with his trunk.
Aaron still sleeps near any little elephant that needs him, keeping watch and feeding him or her around the clock. Aaron dreams of a time when all orphan elephants will roam the African plains as free, wild animals — when there will no longer be a need for elephant orphanages.

W: Have you ever wondered what makes a song ⓐsuccessful in the music industry? Researchers may have found one answer. Here’s Paul Harrison reporting from London.

위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: A recent study suggests that people's musical preferences may be affected by changes in weather and seasons.
Researchers examined more than 23,000 songs that ranked highly on UK music charts over a period of 70 years.
Listeners tended to prefer cheerful and energetic music during periods of pleasant weather rather than during colder or wetter months.
The study recommended that musicians should release new songs during warm and sunny weather to ensure their success.

solution:
날씨와 계절이 음악 선호에 영향을 미칠 수 있으므로, 가수가 신곡을 차트 상위권에 올리고 싶다면 노래가 날씨나 계절에 어떻게 어울릴지를 고려하는 것이 좋다고 했을 뿐, 따뜻하고 화창한 날씨에 신곡을 발표하는 것이 성공을 보장한다고 한 것은 아니므로 ④ ‘해당 연구는 음악가들이 성공 가능성을 보장하기 위해 따뜻하고 화창한 날씨에 신곡을 발표해야 한다고 권고했다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 최근 연구는 사람들의 음악 선호도가 날씨와 계절의 변화에 영향을 받을 수 있음을 시사한다.
② 연구자들은 70년에 걸쳐 영국 음악 차트에서 높은 순위를 기록한 23,000곡 이상의 노래를 분석했다.
③ 청취자들은 춥거나 비가 많이 오는 달보다 날씨가 좋은 시기에 밝고 활기찬 음악을 더 선호하는 경향이 있었다.
⑤ 연구 결과는 음악가들이 신곡을 홍보할 때 날씨와 계절적 조건을 고려할 가치가 있을 수 있음을 시사한다.

body:
Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even ⓐcontrol the weather. Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer that could measure temperature. The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! ⓑIt is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues ⓒthat remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we ⓓwould have been in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, ⓔmaking it look like an enormous snowball.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ would have been → would be (‘~가 없다면’이란 뜻으로 현재 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 가정법 과거 구문에서 if가 생략되어 도치된 부사절 ‘Were it not for ~‘가 쓰였으므로, 주절의 시제를 가정법 과거(주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 ~)로 일치시켜야 한다. 따라서 would have been을 would be로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ have allowed의 목적격보어로 쓰인 to부정사에서, to에 이어지는 동사원형 track, adapt와 ’A, B, and C’의 구조로 병렬 연결되고 있으므로 동사원형 control은 적절하다.
ⓑ 진주어 to say에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 It은 적절하다.
ⓒ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(remain ~ fossils)을 이끌어 선행사 clues를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.

[1]
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively ⓐwet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally ⓑinterrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. ㉠이 기후 변화가 아니었다면, 그 당시 인류는 아프리카 밖으로 퍼져 나가지 않았을지도 모른다.
[2]
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then (A)[moves / moving] onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its ⓒchief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula ⓓdropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to (B)[have triggered / trigger] the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how ⓔfavorable things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year (C)[is / are] many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ favorable(유리한) → desperate(절망적인)

solution:

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.
윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) A recent study examined roughly 100 paintings by William Turner and Claude Monet. (T/F)
(B) The skies depicted in the paintings became increasingly hazy, although industrial air pollution remained relatively stable. (T/F)
(C) The Industrial Revolution brought unprecedented transformations to the skies of London and Paris. (T/F)
(D) Turner and Monet must have been particularly sensitive to changes in atmospheric conditions during their lifetimes. (T/F)
(E) The research concluded that the hazy skies in Turner’s and Monet’s paintings were mainly the result of changes in their artistic techniques. (T/F)
choices: F-T-F-T-T
T-F-T-F-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-F
T-F-T-T-F
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-T-F이다.
(A) 최근의 한 연구는 William Turner와 Claude Monet의 대략 100점의 그림을 조사했다. (일치)
(B) 산업 대기 오염이 비교적 일정하게 유지되었음에도 불구하고(→증가하면서), 그림에 묘사된 하늘은 점점 더 흐릿해졌다. (불일치)
(C) 산업 혁명은 London과 Paris의 하늘에 전례 없는 변화를 가져왔다. (일치)
(D) Turner와 Monet은 생전에 대기 상태의 변화에 특히 민감했을 것이다. (일치)
(E) 그 연구는 Turner와 Monet의 그림 속 흐릿한 하늘이 주로 그들의 예술적 기법의 변화로 인한(→환경의 변화를 반영한) 것이라고 결론 내렸다. (불일치)

One of the most famous pieces of art in the world may have been inspired by an unusual weather event. A study suggests that the sky depicted in Edvard Munch’s The Scream may actually be an accurate representation of a weather phenomenon known as “Mother of Pearl Clouds,” a rare phenomenon that may have a big impact on anyone who sees it for the first time. The typical colors in this rare weather event are the same as the colors in Munch’s painting, and the circumstances under which these rare clouds form match Munch’s environment at the time he conceived The Scream.

During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. body:
Fog Saves the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain ⓐhad increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely (A)[agree / disagree] that Washington would ⓑbe surely captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.
A Weather Phenomenon Inspires a Famous Painting
One of the most famous pieces of art in the world may have been inspired by an unusual weather event. A study suggests ⓒthat the sky depicted in Edvard Munch’s The Scream may actually be a(n) (B)[accurate / distorted] representation of a weather phenomenon known as “Mother of Pearl Clouds,” a rare phenomenon that may have a big impact on anyone who ⓓsees it for the first time. The typical colors in this rare weather event are the same as the colors in Munch’s painting, and the circumstances ⓔwhich these rare clouds form (C)[contradict / match] Munch’s environment at the time he conceived The Scream.

(A) (B) (C)
choices: disagree / accurate / contradict
agree / distorted / contradict

solution:

disagree ~에 동의하지 않다
(B) ‘자개구름’이라 불리는 기상 현상의 전형적인 색상은 Munch의 그림 속 색상과 같다고 했으므로 ‘절규’에 그려진 하늘이 실제로 ‘자개구름’이라는 기상 현상을 정확히 표현한 것이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 accurate(정확한)가 적절하다.
distorted 왜곡된
