contradict ~와 모순되다

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways ⓐto influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
There have been two main approaches aimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even ⓑadd highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere more reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it reaches the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would ⓒbe fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or breaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials. For example, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to fertilize ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while taking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ ⓓemitting into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and isolate CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. Still, some believe ⓔthat we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Climate engineering includes methods for reflecting sunlight and removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
Making the earth’s surface more reflective can reduce the amount of sunlight that contributes to global warming.
Reflective particles are released into clouds to absorb sunlight and increase the heat reaching the earth’s surface.
Ocean planktons take in carbon dioxide as they grow and carry some of the carbon to the ocean floor.
Considering the energy consumed in carbon capture, the process could reduce total global emissions by no more than one-tenth.

오답
① 기후 공학은 햇빛을 반사하고 대기에서 이산화탄소를 제거하는 방법을 포함한다.

④ 해양 플랑크톤은 성장하면서 이산화탄소를 흡수하고 탄소의 일부를 해저로 운반한다.
⑤ 탄소 포집에 소모되는 에너지를 고려하면, 이 과정은 전 세계 총배출량을 최대 10분의 1만큼 줄일 수 있다.

M: Hi, Sumi. Well, I’m feeling a bit under the weather today.
ⓐ Oh, “feeling under the weather” means feeling slightly ill or being in low spirits. I’m afraid I might have caught a cold or something.
ⓑ What do you mean? The forecast says the weather will be fine today.
ⓒ I’m sorry to hear that.
ⓓ Oh, don’t worry. I’m just feeling a bit down. That’s all.
G: I’m curious where the expression “feel under the weather” came from. Maybe from the fact that bad weather can make you sick?
M: Possibly. Or some suggest that it came from the old sailing ships. They say if a sailor was feeling ill, he would be sent below deck to protect him from the weather.
G: That’s very interesting. Come to think of it, there are many idioms about weather in Korean, too.
M: There must be. Those expressions show how closely the weather and our lives are connected.
G: You said it. By the way, I hope you get well soon, or may I say, lightning fast.
M: There you go. Thanks!

There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet ⓐwas most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is ⓑbelieved to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, ⓒmeant conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts ⓓthat lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not ⓔspread outside of Africa.

body:
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics ⓐwhat were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which ⓑinvolve cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found ⓒthat, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, ⓓseems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how desperate things ⓔhad become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many ⓕcarved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ what → that (주어가 없는 불완전한 절(were ~ time)을 이끌어 선행사 advances in mathematics를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 주격 관계대명사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓑ involve → involves (콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 slash-and-burn agriculture를 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 선행사 slash-and-burn agriculture가 단수명사구이므로 이에 수일치하도록 involve를 단수동사 involves로 고친다.)

Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even control the weather. In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. (C) However, modern technological solutions to environmental issues often fail to address the fundamental causes of global climate change. (D) But far more often than we control the weather, the weather controls us. (E) The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 인류가 역사적으로 날씨를 추적하고 적응하며 제어하기 위해 다양한 기술을 발전시켜 왔지만, 실제로는 날씨와 기후가 인류의 삶과 역사에 더 큰 영향을 미쳐 왔다는 내용의 글이다. (A)와 (B)에서는 인류가 날씨를 제어하기 위해 사용한 기술의 사례를 제시하고, (D)에서는 인류가 날씨를 제어하는 경우보다 날씨가 인류에게 영향을 미치는 경우가 훨씬 더 많다고 하며 글의 흐름을 전환하고, (E)에서는 날씨와 기후가 강제 이주, 전쟁, 예술 작품 창작 등 인류 역사의 중대한 사건에 영향을 미쳤음을 구체적으로 설명한다. 반면 (C) ‘그러나 현대의 환경 문제에 대한 기술적 해결책은 종종 지구 기후 변화의 근본적인 원인을 다루는 데 실패한다.’는 날씨를 제어하려는 인류의 시도와 그보다 더 큰 날씨가 인류에게 미치는 영향을 다루는 글의 중심 흐름에서 벗어나므로 (C)는 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, where British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, had it not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, which made the United States an independent nation.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

The Surprising Impact of Climate Conditions on the American Revolution
Military Strategies That Led Washington to Victory over British Forces
Why British Forces Struggled to Maintain Control over the Colonies
The Long, Tough Journey to American Independence

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more (A)______ the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often (B)______ realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

(A) largely indifferent to (B) distinguished from
(A) largely indifferent to (B) contrasted with
(A) highly sensitive to (B) associated with
(A) acutely conscious of (B) distinguished from

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways to influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
There have been two main approaches aimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth. On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface (A)[darker / brighter] by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere more reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it (B)[reaches / leaves] the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would be fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or breaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials. For example, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to (C)[deplete / fertilize] ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while taking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ emitted into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and isolate CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. Still, some believe that we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) brighter (B) reaches (C) fertilize
(A) darker (B) leaves (C) fertilize
(A) brighter (B) reaches (C) deplete
(A) darker (B) reaches (C) deplete
(A) brighter (B) leaves (C) deplete
solution:
(A) 지표면에서 햇빛을 반사하기 위해 지붕을 흰색으로 칠하거나 사막에 반사율이 높은 덮개를 설치한다고 했으므로 지구 표면의 밝기가 증가시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 brighter(더 밝은)가 적절하다.
(B) 지구 온난화를 막기 위한 접근법을 설명하는 것이므로 태양의 빛이 지표면에 도달하기 전에 산란한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reaches(~에 도달하다)가 적절하다.
(C) 뒤에서 플랑크톤이 성장하면서 대기 중 이산화탄소를 흡수하고, 일부 탄소를 포함한 상태로 바다 바닥에 가라앉는다고 했으므로 해양 플랑크톤의 성장을 촉진한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 fertilize(~의 성장을 촉진하다)가 적절하다.

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because ______. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of how desperate things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: local farmers had developed effective methods of preventing soil erosion
the soil naturally retained moisture throughout the year
seasonal floods serves as a reliable source of water
rivers provided sufficient water for farming
rain was its chief water source
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Earth Cools and Warms Before Human History
The earth was formed about 4.5 billion years ago — that is a very long time ago! It is hard to say exactly what the weather was like in any particular place on any particular day thousands or millions of years ago. But we know a lot about what the earth’s climate was like way back then, thanks to clues that remain in rocks, ice, trees, and fossils. Were it not for these natural records of the past, we would be in the dark as to the climate of the long past.
About 55-56 million years ago, the global mean temperature appears to have been as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.
Climate Change Drives Humans out of Africa
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. (A)호모 사피엔스는 20만 년 전보다 이전의 어느 시점에 동아프리카에서 진화한 것으로 여겨진다. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The earth’s ancient climate can be investigated through traces preserved in various parts of the natural environment.
Scientists have difficulty determining the weather conditions of an exact place and date from millions of years ago.
Palm trees and crocodiles lived in regions beyond the Arctic Circle when the polar regions were free of ice caps.
For most of its history, the earth was colder than it is today, with only rare periods of higher temperatures.
The movement of early humans beyond Africa was probably made possible by periods when climate conditions provided greater access to essential resources.

Throughout human history, inventions and technological advances have allowed people to track, adapt to, and even control the weather. (A) Around 1602, Galileo first conceptualized a thermometer that could measure temperature. (B) The air conditioner made its first appearance in 1902. (C) In 1946, researchers succeeded in producing rain clouds over the sky of Massachusetts. (D) The weather — or more broadly, the climate — has caused significant events throughout human history, from forced migration or the course of a war to even the creation of famous artworks. (E)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘하지만 우리가 날씨를 제어하기보다는 날씨가 우리를 훨씬 더 많이 제어한다.’라는 뜻으로, 주어진 문장에 But이 쓰였으므로 이 문장 앞에는 인류가 날씨를 제어해 온 내용이, 이 문장 뒤에는 날씨가 인류를 제어하는 내용이 와야 한다. (B) 앞에서 갈릴레오가 최초의 온도계를 구상하고, (C) 앞에서 1902년에 최초의 에어컨이 등장하며, (D) 앞에서 과학자들이 매사추세츠 상공에 비구름을 만든 사례를 통해 인류가 날씨를 제어해 온 과정을 보여 주고 있다. 반면 (D) 뒤에서는 강제 이주, 전쟁, 예술 작품 창작 등 인류 역사 전반에 걸쳐 날씨가 영향을 미친 사례를 제시하고 있으므로, 인류의 날씨 제어에서 날씨의 인류 제어로 글의 흐름이 전환되는 (D)에 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

body:
B: Mom, I’m home. (A)I can’t stand this hot weather!
W: You’ve had a tough time outside, huh? It really seems the earth is getting hotter and hotter every year.
B: I’m going to turn on the air conditioner right away. I’ll close all the windows first.
W: Wait! Why don’t we leave the windows open just for a short while? I read that it’s better to keep them open for some time after you turn on the air conditioner.
B: Why is that?
W: The hot air in the house needs to be pushed out first, especially on a very hot day like this.
B: I see what you mean.
W: Let’s set the temperature at around 26 degrees.
B: At 26? Why so high? Why don’t we choose a very low temperature to cool the air quickly and then turn the air conditioner off?
W: Well, we can actually save more energy by keeping the air conditioner on at a moderate temperature and not turning it on and off frequently.
B: Okay. Then, if it doesn’t feel cool enough, I’ll use the fan, too.
W: Sounds good! You know, saving energy is saving the earth.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: I’m not happy about this hot weather.
This hot weather is very annoying.
I’m annoyed by this hot weather.
I don't mind this hot weather.
I'm used to this hot weather.
solution:
‘I can’t stand ~‘는 ‘~을 정말 못 참겠다’라는 의미로, 어떤 상황, 행동 등에 대해 더 이상 참을 수 없을 만큼 화나거나 싫어하는 감정을 표현할 때 사용하며, ‘I’m not happy about ~‘ ’I’m annoyed by ~‘ ’~ is very annoying.‘과 같은 표현으로도 화나거나 싫어하는 감정을 나타낼 수 있다. ‘I don't mind ~’는 ‘~을 신경 쓰지 않는다’라는 뜻이고, I'm used to+명사(구)’는 ‘~에 익숙하다’를 뜻하므로 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은 ④ ‘이 더운 날씨를 신경 쓰지 않아요.’, ⑤ ‘이 더운 날씨에 익숙해요’이다.
오답
① 이 더운 날씨가 마음에 들지 않아요.
② 이 더운 날씨는 너무 짜증나게 해요.
③ 이 더운 날씨 때문에 짜증나요.

About 55-56 million years ago, ⓑthe global mean temperature appears to be as high as 23°C, while today’s global average is just shy of 19°C. During much of this hot period, the North and South Poles were free of ice caps, and palm trees and crocodiles lived above the Arctic Circle.
While our planet has been hotter — sometimes much hotter — than it is today for much of its history, it has also been colder at times. When deep freezes occurred between 750 and 600 million years ago, ice covered the entire surface of the earth, making it look like an enormous snowball.

Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that ⓐwere far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region ⓑthat depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, ⓒcombined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans ⓓthemselves left behind a clue of how desperate things had become. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year ⓔis many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ is → are (장소를 나타내는 부사구 ‘Among ~ year‘가 강조를 위해 문장의 맨 앞으로 이동하면 1형식 동사와 주어는 도치된다. 따라서 문장의 주어는 뒤에 이어지는 복수명사구 many carved stones이므로 이에 수일치하여 단수동사 is를 복수동사 are로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하며, 선행사 advances in mathematics가 복수명사구이므로 이에 수일치한 복수동사 were는 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(depended ~ systems)을 이끌어 명사구 a region을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다.
ⓒ 뒤에 동사 seems가 있으므로, 이중 콤마(,)로 주어인 The drought을 부연 설명하는 분사구가 삽입된 형태로, 명사구 The drought가 전쟁 및 다른 갈등과 ’결합된‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 combined는 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어 The Mayans를 강조하여 ’마야인들 자신이‘라는 뜻으로 쓰였으므로, 복수형 재귀대명사 themselves는 적절하다.

body:
Fog Saves the American Revolution
By the summer of 1776, Britain had increased its troop strength to more than 30,000 in a battle against General George Washington’s 19,000-man army for control of New York City. Washington moved the revolutionaries out to Brooklyn and Queens, (A)[which / where] British soldiers began their attack. Americans secretly made their way across the East River, totally undetected by the British soldiers just a few hundred meters away because of a dense fog cover. Historians widely agree that Washington would have surely been captured and punished as a traitor by the British government, (B)[had it / it had] not been for that fog. Instead, the American Revolution ended in victory for the new colonies, (C)[what / which] made the United States an independent nation.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) / (B) / (C)
choices: where / it had / which
which / had it / which
where / had it / what
where / had it / which
which / it had / what
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(British ~ attack)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 장소를 나타내는 선행사 Brooklyn and Queens를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.
(B) ‘~이 없었다면’이라는 뜻의 과거 사실과 반대되는 상황(그 안개가 없었다면)을 가정하는 가정법 과거완료구문은 ‘if it had not been for ~’ 또는 if를 생략한 도치구문 ‘had it not been for ~’의 형태로 쓰이며, that 뒤에서 두 완전한 절이 접속사 없이 연결될 수 없으므로 if가 생략된 형태임을 알 수 있다. 따라서 도치된 had it이 적절하다.
(C) 불완전한 절(made ~ nation)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 절 전체를 선행사로 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.

body:
While there have been generations of efforts to adjust weather in our favor, most of them were more theatrical than effective. However, some scientists began seriously considering ways to influence the climate system itself in an emerging field, most widely known today as “climate engineering” or “climate intervention” efforts.
(A) On the ground level, it may involve making the earth’s surface brighter by painting the roof tops white or even adding highly reflective coverings across large areas of desert. On the atmospheric level, it works by making the atmosphere ⓐmore reflective so that the sun’s light is scattered before it reaches the earth’s surface. To achieve this, bright, reflective particles would be fired into clouds using airplanes or balloons flying high in the sky.
(B) There have been two main approaches ⓑaimed at preventing undesired warming. One centers on slowing down global warming by reflecting some of the sun’s rays back into space before they can warm the earth.
(C) The other approach is focused on capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and storing it underground, or ⓒbreaking down CO₂ molecules and locking the carbon in stable materials.
For example, iron dust is scattered from ships in order to fertilize ocean planktons. As these organisms grow, they consume carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, and sink to the ocean floor while ⓓtaking some of the carbon with them. On the ocean floor, the carbon can stay for hundreds of years.
There are, however, a host of issues too, ranging from technical to ethical to diplomatic. Perhaps the biggest issue is simply the scale of emissions — the enormous amount of CO₂ emitted into the atmosphere every year. Against such reality, could the climate engineering efforts make a difference? A recent study found that after taking into account the energy used to capture and ⓔisolating CO₂, the carbon capture efforts would reduce the total global emissions by at most 10%. Still, some believe that we need to pursue multiple routes to slow climate change. Even if there is no 100% solution, they say, we need a lot of 10% and 20% solutions.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 최근 과학자들이 기후 시스템 자체에 영향을 미치는 ‘기후 공학’ 연구를 본격화하고 있다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 기후 공학의 두 가지 주요 접근법이 있으며 그 첫 번째 접근법인 태양 광선을 반사하여 지구 온난화를 늦추는 방법을 설명하는 (B), 첫 번째 접근법인 태양 광선을 반사하는 구체적인 방법 중 지상에서(On the ground level) 실행하는 방안과 대기 수준에서(On the atmospheric level) 실행하는 방안을 구체적으로 설명하는 (A), 다른 접근법인 이산화탄소를 포집하여 지하에 저장하거나 분해하는 것을 설명하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ isolating → isolate 또는 to isolate (흐름상 ‘이산화탄소를 포집하고 분리하는 데 사용되는’을 뜻하므로 to부정사 to capture와 등위접속사 and로 병렬로 연결되어야 한다. 따라서 isolating을 to부정사 to isolate 또는 to를 생략한 동사원형 isolate로 고친다.)
*본문에서는 isolate가 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 동명사 making의 목적격보어 자리이며 making은 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)(~을 …하게 만들다)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 making의 목적격보어로 쓰인 비교급 형용사 more reflective는 적절하다.

ⓒ focused on의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사구 capturing ~ underground와 등위접속사 or로 병렬 연결되며 동시에 뒤에 위치한 동명사 locking과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되므로 동명사 breaking은 적절하다.
ⓓ 접속사 while 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 접속사를 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어 some of the carbon이 이어지므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 taking은 적절하다.

body:
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution increased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution transformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental changes, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the atmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather accurately, a reality of environmental changes.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
A recent study of paintings by Turner and Monet revealed that the increasingly hazy ______ depicted in their works reflected rising industrial ______ ______ during the Industrial Revolution demonstrating that ______ ______ accurately captured environmental changes although ______ is generally viewed as distinct from realism.
answer: skies, air pollution, impressionist artists, impressionism
solution: 요약문 Turner와 Monet의 그림들에 대한 최근 연구는 그들의 작품에 묘사된 점점 더 흐릿해지는 하늘이 산업혁명 동안 증가하는 산업 대기 오염을 반영했다는 것을 밝혀냈으며, 이는 인상주의가 일반적으로 사실주의와 구별되는 것으로 여겨지지만 인상주의 화가들이 환경 변화를 정확하게 포착했음을 보여준다.

body:
There is no greater decider of human history than climate change, due to its long-term effect on living conditions. Scientists have discovered that humanity’s earliest move out of Africa and into other reaches of the planet was most likely due to climate change. Homo sapiens is believed to have evolved in eastern Africa sometime over 200,000 years ago. For a long time, the climate of eastern Africa was relatively wet, meaning conditions were favorable for them with plenty of food and water available. From 125,000 years ago, however, the climate gradually became drier in eastern Africa. This long-term drying trend was occasionally interrupted by climate shifts that lasted a few thousand years. In particular, the wet period that occurred 62,000 to 60,000 years ago throughout the Arabian and Sinai peninsulas created clear migration paths by providing sufficient food and water resources. If it had not been for the climate shifts, the humans of that time might not have spread outside of Africa.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Significance of Natural Resources in Supporting Human Survival
Effects of Long-Term Drought on African Food and Water Supplies
Changing Climate Patterns That Paved the Way for Early Human Migration
How Ancient Climate Changes Influenced the Evolution of Homo sapiens
The Fundamental Factors Revealed by Early Human Settlement Patterns

body:
Drought Spells the End for the Mayan Civilization
During its peak around 800 A.D., the Mayan civilization was responsible for astonishing stone temples, highly advanced astronomical observatories, and advances in mathematics that were far ahead of its time. The Mayans also practiced slash-and-burn agriculture, which involves cutting down a forest, burning the entire area, farming on the rich soil for a couple of years, and then moving onto a new plot. This method led to extreme deforestation in the Yucatán Peninsula, a region that depended on underground root systems to maintain water resources because rain was its chief water source. Researchers found that, over 200 years, rainfall in the Yucatán Peninsula dropped by as much as 70%. The drought, combined with wars and other conflicts, seems to have triggered the end of the Mayan civilization. The Mayans themselves left behind a clue of ______. Among the ruins that attract thousands of tourists each year are many carved stones in the shape of Chaac, the rain god of the Mayan culture.
*slash-and-burn agriculture 화전 농업

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how ineffective their scientific achievements were in preventing the civilization’s decline
how greatly declining rainfall affected their agricultural practices
how significantly their conflicts contributed to the civilization’s decline
how seriously deforestation threatened their water resources
how desperately they longed for rain to save them

body:
Air Pollution Brings the Hazy, Dreamy Impressionist Skies
A recent study analyzed the changes in style and color of nearly 100 paintings by impressionists William Turner and Claude Monet, who lived during Europe’s Industrial Revolution in the 18th and 19th centuries. The study found that over time, as industrial air pollution ⓐincreased throughout Turner’s and Monet’s careers, the skies in their paintings became hazier, too. The Industrial Revolution ⓑtransformed the skies of London and Paris, the painters’ hometowns, in unprecedented ways. Many artists draw inspiration from surrounding environmental ⓒstability, and impressionist artists like Turner and Monet must have been more keenly aware of the ⓓatmospheric changes of their time. While impressionism is often contrasted with realism, the study pointed out that Turner’s and Monet’s works had captured a certain reality rather ⓔaccurately, a reality of environmental changes.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓒ stability(안정성) → changes(변화들)

W: Good evening everyone! Welcome to our show. Today, we have a special guest with us, Benjamin Shine.
M: Hi, thank you for having me.
W: Your work is truly fascinating. Your face portraits appear to come out of thin air. It seems that each of your portraits is painted in one color only.
M: No. They are not painted. I make faces with fabric. I just need a single piece of fabric, an iron, and a lot of work.
W: Drawing with fabric! That's surprising! Now I see that they're all fabric. Could you explain how you create one of your portraits?
M: Sure. First, I draw the outline of a face with a pencil. Then, I use the iron and fold the fabric to create faces. After that, I keep pressing and pinching the fabric.
W: What inspires you to create them?
M: ______ I think my inspirations come from the beauty of the human face. I love exploring facial expressions and the emotions they convey.
W: That's impressive. Thank you so much for joining us today and for sharing your incredible work with us.
M: It's been a pleasure.

body:
Cloth That Connected the Worlds
It is said ⓐthat silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea ⓑhad dissolved the coating of the cocoon. ⓒThat she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.
For a long time, silk was a material ⓓreserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk ⓔwas eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, prompting the development of the civilizations.

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Who is said to have discovered silk production?
What happened to the cocoon when it fell into a cup?
Why were the restrictions on who could wear and use silk relaxed?
What is considered the earliest evidence of the silk trade?
What else was exchanged along the Silk Road besides silk?

body:
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, (A)달에서 입었던 각각의 우주복은 약 4,000개의 직물 조각과 21겹의 다른 재료로 이루어졌고, 당시 무게가 72 kg에 달했다. It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: More than 500 million people watched the moment when humans first stepped onto the moon.
The Apollo suits had to withstand extremely high and low temperatures.
NASA chose the company that had earned its reputation by producing women’s underwear.
Using their hands and sewing machines, skilled seamstresses produced the suits mainly from fabric.
NASA’s advanced technology greatly helped the seamstresses create the simplest space suits ever used.
solution:
아폴로 우주복은 지금까지 사용된 우주복 가운데 가장 복잡한 우주복으로 남아 있으며, 그것은 NASA의 기술적 전문 지식보다 속옷을 꿰매고 만들면서 단련된 여성들의 솜씨가 만들어 낸 결실이었다고 했으므로, ⑤ ‘NASA의 고도의 기술은 재봉사들이, 지금까지 사용된 가장 단순한 우주복을 만드는 데 큰 도움을 주었다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 5억 명이 넘는 사람들이 인간이 처음 달에 발을 디딘 순간을 지켜보았다.
② 아폴로 우주복은 극도로 높고 낮은 온도를 견뎌야 했다.
③ NASA는 여성 속옷을 생산하여 명성을 얻은 회사를 선택했다.
④ 숙련된 재봉사들은 그들의 손과 재봉틀을 사용하여 주로 직물로 우주복을 제작했다.

body:
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits ______. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive edge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. However, since most sports require equipment of some sort, it can be tricky to determine what is technology doping and what is not. Some argue that it is a natural progress coming from scientific development, while others claim it undermines human spirit and effort, ensuring that rich athletes have an advantage over poor ones.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
choices: reached the physical limits of human endurance
faced unexpected safety hazards in deep water
stopped wearing the suits to maintain fairness
returned to wearing traditional swimsuits
continued to break world records
solution:
베이징 올림픽에서 25개의 세계 신기록 중 23개가 새로운 전신 수영복 착용에 의해 세워졌다고 했고, 빈칸 뒤에서 그 결과, 2009년에 FINA가 전신 수영복 착용을 금지하기로 결정했다고 했으므로 혁신적인 수영복을 입은 선수들이 계속해서 기록을 갈아치웠다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘계속해서 세계 기록을 깼다’가 적절하다.
오답

Have you ever imagined painting with clothes, not on clothes? Surprisingly, Ian Berry succeeded in this and makes art out of blue jeans. His art looks like a painting, but people suddenly notice the beauty in blue jeans when they look at his art. He collects denim of every shade and uses it to create the shading and the sense of perspective in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art. With just his hands, scissors, and glue, he creates almost three-dimensional pieces. He ⓑhas been making realistic installations of denim for many years. He uses discarded jeans, cuts them up into pieces, and, like a painter, ⓒsorting them according to color. At first glance, the work seems flat, but a closer look reveals different layers of denim ⓓplaced on top of and over each other. They are in fact denim collages. They are almost impossible ⓔto distinguish from paintings.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ sorting → sorts (단수동사 uses, cuts와 함께 ‘A, B, and C’의 형태로 병렬을 이루어야 하므로 sorting을 단수동사 sorts로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘be used+to부정사(~하는 데 사용되다)’의 의미로, 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to draw는 적절하다.
ⓑ 과거부터 시작해서 현재까지 계속되고 있고, 지금도 진행 중인 것을 표현하기 위해 현재완료진행 시제 have been -ing는 적절하다.
ⓓ 명사구 different layers of denim을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, different layers of denim이 ‘놓여진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 placed는 적절하다.
ⓔ ‘구분하기가 (불가능한)’라는 뜻으로 형용사 impossible을 수식하므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to distinguish는 적절하다.

body:
What to Wear for Space Travel
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit (A)[what / that] could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand ⓐextreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not ⓑexist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so ⓒhard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, (B)[weighed / weighing] 72 kg at the time. It remains the most ⓓplain space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the ⓔcraftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and (C)[making / made] underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓓ plain(단순한) → complex(복잡한)

body:
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many woven around the production of silk.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
According to one of many stories, ______ ______ is believed to have been started when Leizu discovered ______ ______ from a ______ in her tea and turned them into a soft, shiny, cool ______.
answer: silk production, soft fibers, cocoon, fabric
solution: 요약문 많은 이야기 중 하나에 따르면, 비단 생산은 Leizu가 자신의 차의 고치로부터 나온 부드러운 섬유를 발견하고 그것들을 부드럽고 반짝이며 시원한 직물로 만들었을 때 시작되었다고 여겨진다.

body:
Technology Doping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers.
(A) In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits.
(B) It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air.
(C) In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit.
They also dictated that the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 25개의 수영 세계 신기록이 수립된 2008년 베이징 올림픽에서 많은 수영 선수들이 새로운 유형의 수영복을 입었다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 앞서 언급된 새로운 유형의 수영복을 대명사 it으로 이어받아 상어 피부를 모방한 소재로 만들어진 전신 수영복의 특징을 구체적으로 설명하는 (B), (B)의 마지막 부분에서 이 수영복이 부력을 높여준다는 내용이 제시된 뒤, In fact(실제로)를 통해 부력을 높이기 위해 이 수영복(these suits)을 여러 벌 착용한 실제 사례와 해당 수영복을 입은 선수들이 베이징 올림픽에서 세운 세계 기록의 결과를 제시하는 (C), (C)에서 베이징 올림픽 당시의 기록을 설명한 뒤, 베이징 올림픽 이후 대회들에서(In later competitions) 혁신적인 수영복을 착용한 선수들이 계속해서 세계 신기록을 경신했다는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used to draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
People usually take pictures of scenic views, but Teresa Lim paints pictures of tourist spots with a needle and thread when she travels the world. She embroiders places she visits in surprising detail. This method of preserving memories lets her truly take in her surroundings. She spends time sitting in one place, observing details and stitching as the scene reveals itself. She says on her website that her designs “seek to erase the lines and boundaries between being an illustrator and a textile designer.” Her art is a delightful fusion of a canvas and a camera that projects travel scenes onto fabric. She recreates what she sees on cloth and eliminates the need for a vacation photo album.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the creative use of textiles to create unique works of art
the practical advantages of taking photographs while traveling
the growing popularity of traditional embroidery among modern artists
the importance of accurately copying scenic views in textile design
the differences between photography and painting as ways to record travel memories
solution:
다양한 스타일과 종류의 직물이 예술에서 사용될 수 있으며, 그 예시로 Teresa Lim은 여행지의 모습을 사진 대신 바늘과 실로 세밀하게 자수하고, 주변을 관찰하며 여행의 추억을 기록하는 예술 작품을 만든다고 했으므로 이 글의 주제로 ① ‘독특한 예술 작품으로 바뀌는 섬유의 창의적 활용’이 적절하다.

② 여행 중 사진을 찍는 것의 실용적인 장점
③ 현대 예술가들 사이에서 전통적인 자수의 증가하는 인기
④ 직물 디자인에서 풍경을 정확하게 모방하는 것의 중요성

G: Your bag looks so beautiful, and the picture on it is very interesting. Where did you buy it?
B: I didn't buy this bag. I made it by myself last week. I went on a field trip to the Museum of Craft Art and took a textile art class there.
G: Textile art? I didn't know you were interested in that.
B: The Museum of Craft Art offered some classes to learn about textile crafting.
G: It sounds great. How was the class? Were you satisfied with it?
B: Yes, I was. When I finished making my own bag, I felt proud of myself. Making something by using fabric and thread with my own hands was exciting.
G: Wasn't it difficult to learn?
B: It was difficult to follow the manual at first, but I soon got the hang of handling the thread and fabric.
G: Your bag is one of a kind. It must be so meaningful to you.
B: You're right. I feel great every time I carry my bag.

The boy considers his bag meaningful and feels good whenever he carries it.

body:
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk were eased, and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. What to Wear for Space Travel
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest ⓐchallenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits ⓑwasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses ⓒusing their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard ⓓwas the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit ⓔwas worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to ⓕhave used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

6개

body:
Technology Doping
During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were set. (A) At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. (B) The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. (C) In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to increase buoyancy. (D) In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers wearing this type of suit. (E)
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to ban all full body swimsuits. ⓐ그들은 또한 수영복을 만들기 위해 쓰이는 직물은 통기성이 있어야 한다고 규정했다.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
It was a full body swimsuit designed with a material that imitated shark skin.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그것은 상어의 피부를 모방한 소재로 디자인된 전신 수영복이었다.’라는 뜻으로, 대명사 It을 사용하여 앞에서 언급된 수영복이 구체적으로 어떤 종류의 수영복인지 설명하고 있다. 따라서 이 문장 앞에는 수영복의 존재나 종류만 언급되고, 그 수영복의 소재나 구체적인 특징은 아직 제시되지 않은 문장이 오는 것이 적절하다. (B) 앞에서 2008년 베이징 올림픽에서 새로운 유형의 수영복(a new type of swimsuit)이 많은 수영선수들에 의해 착용되었다는 사실만 언급되었을 뿐, 그 수영복이 구체적으로 어떤 수영복인지는 설명되지 않았다. 따라서 (B)에 주어진 문장이 오면 a new type of swimsuit를 대명사 It으로 이어받아, 그것이 전신 수영복(a full ~ shark skin)임을 구체적으로 설명하며, (B) 뒤의 The suit는 바로 앞에서 설명한 수영복을 다시 가리켜 그 수영복의 효과와 특징(산소 공급 향상, 물의 저항 감소, 부력 증가)에 대한 설명으로 자연스럽게 이어지므로 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (B)이다.

body:
Various styles and types of textiles can be used in art. In textile art, blue jeans, not water paints, can be used to draw pictures. Beautiful threads replace photos of scenic views. These types of textiles can be brilliant tools for expanding artistic creativity.
Ian Berry, Denim Art
Have you ever imagined painting with clothes, not on clothes? Surprisingly, Ian Berry succeeded in this and makes art out of blue jeans. His art looks like a painting, but people suddenly notice the beauty in blue jeans when they look at his art. He collects denim of every shade and uses it to create the shading and the sense of perspective in his portraits, landscapes, and other unique works of art. With just his hands, scissors, and glue, he creates almost three-dimensional pieces. He (A)[has been making / has been made] realistic installations of denim for many years. He uses discarded jeans, cuts them up into pieces, and, like a painter, sorts them according to color. At first glance, the work seems flat, but a closer look reveals different layers of denim placed on top of and over each other. They are in fact denim collages. They are almost impossible to distinguish from paintings.
Teresa Lim, Embroidery Art
People usually take pictures of scenic views, but Teresa Lim paints pictures of tourist spots with a needle and thread when she travels the world. She embroiders places (B)[what / that] she visits in surprising detail. This method of preserving memories lets her truly take in her surroundings. She spends time sitting in one place, observing details and stitching as the scene reveals itself. She says on her website that her designs “seek to erase the lines and boundaries between being an illustrator and a textile designer.” Her art is a delightful fusion of a canvas and a camera that (C)[project / projects] travel scenes onto fabric. She recreates what she sees on cloth and eliminates the need for a vacation photo album.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: has been made / that / project
has been making / that / projects
has been making / what / project
has been made / what / projects
has been making / that / project
solution:
(A) 주어 He가 사실적인 설치 미술품을 지금까지 ‘만들어 온’ 주체이자, 지금도 계속 만들고 있는 중임을 강조하기 위해, 현재완료진행(have/has been+-ing)인 has been making이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
(B) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(she ~ detail)을 이끌어 선행사 places를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하므로, 선행사인 단수 명사구 ‘a delightful ~ camera’에 수일치한 단수동사 projects는 적절하다.

We live surrounded by cloth. We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. Textiles ─artificial and natural ─have shaped and changed the world we live in. The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more (A)[enriched / enriching]. Exploring ⓐ______ helps us understand how human civilization has evolved.
[2]
For a long time, silk was a material reserved for the Emperor and those very close to him. Gradually, the restrictions on who could wear and use silk (B)[eased / were eased], and more and more people could be seen to wear silk clothing and to dress up their homes with silk decorations. Eventually, silk production grew to become quite a large industry in China.
Silk became a valuable commodity highly sought after by other countries at a very early time, and it is believed that the silk trade was actually started before the Silk Road was officially opened in the second century B.C. The threads of silk found in the hair of an Egyptian mummy from around 1070 B.C. are probably the earliest evidence of the silk trade. The Silk Road significantly shaped the societies and cultures of the regions that it connected. Not only silk, but spices, rare metals, and exotic animals were also exchanged on the road. Religions, artistic styles, and technologies were shared as well, prompting the development of the civilizations.
[3]
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s surprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to (C)[have been used / be used] to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: enriched / were eased / be used
enriching / eased / have been used
enriching / were eased / be used
enriched / eased / have been used
enriched / were eased / have been used
solution:
(A) be동사의 현재완료형 has been에 이어지는 주격보어 자리이며, 주어 it(=The history of textiles)이 점점 더 ‘풍부해진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 enriched가 적절하다.
(B) 주어 the restrictions에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, the restrictions가 ‘느슨해진’ 대상이므로 수동태(be+p.p.) were eased가 적절하다.
(C) 더 이전부터 지금까지 사용되어 온 것을 강조하여 나타내기 위해 완료 시제를 사용한 ’to have+p.p.’인 have been used가 적절하다.

(A) 전신 수영복의 특징으로, 근육으로의 산소 공급 향상, 부력 증가와 함께 선수들이 물속에서 더 좋은 경기력을 낼 수 있도록 하는 기능이 이어져야 하므로 물의 저항을 감소시킨다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reduced(감소된)가 적절하다.
(B) 앞에서 새로운 전신 수영복이 공기를 가둬 부력을 높였고, 이 수영복을 입은 선수들이 계속해서 세계 기록을 깼다고 했으므로 이를 규제하기 위해 FINA가 수영복의 직물은 통기성이 있도록 규정한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 breathable(통기성이 있는)이 적절하다.
(C) ‘기술 도핑’이 정정당당한 경쟁에 반하는 것일 수 있다고 언급하며, 기술 도핑을 비판하는 사람들은 그것이 인간의 정신력과 노력을 약화시킨다고 주장하므로, 기술 도핑이 부유한 선수들이 가난한 선수들보다 유리하도록 보장한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ensuring(확실히 하는)이 적절하다.

body:
It is said that silk production began with the most Chinese of things: tea. Leizu, the young wife of the Yellow Emperor, was sitting under a tree, with a cup of tea in her hand. A cocoon fell from one of the branches directly into the cup. Naturally, she fished the offending object out, and to her amazement, she found that the tea had dissolved the coating of the cocoon. What she held was a little lump of soft fibers. Leizu unraveled it until it stretched from end to end of her garden, over 600 meters. Intrigued, she gathered more cocoons from the tree to unravel, and worked the threads into cloth. The result was a soft and shiny fabric that was cool to the touch. This Chinese legend is only one of many ______

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: woven around the production of silk
confirmed by researchers as historically accurate
made by accident in the field of textile engineering
developed to explain the origins of traditional tea culture
passed down to describe the invention of Chinese agriculture
solution: 앞에서 비단 생산에 대해 Leizu와 누에고치에 관한 이야기를 소개한 뒤 ‘This Chinese legend(이 중국의 전설은)이라고 시작하므로, 이 전설이 비단 생산의 기원을 둘러싼 여러 전설 중 하나라는 내용이 이어지는 것이 가장 자연스럽다. 따라서 ❶ '비단 생산을 둘러싸고 만들어진'이 적절하다.

body:
We live surrounded by cloth. We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. Textiles ─artificial and natural ─ have ⓐshaped and changed the world we live in. The history of textiles is almost as old as human civilization, and as time has passed, it has been more and more enriched. Exploring how textiles have changed the world helps us understand how human civilization has evolved.
What to Wear for Space Travel
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people ⓑtuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest ⓒchallenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. To everyone’s ⓓsurprise, the company which won the contract for the Apollo suits wasn’t as big as the others and owed its reputation to its product line of female underwear. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most ⓔsimple space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ simple(단순한) → complex(복잡한)

body:
[Alarm goes off.]
G: What was that?
B: Oh, it’s my smartphone telling me that I should go take a walk for at least 30 minutes.
G: Wow! That’s pretty cool.
B: Yeah. This health app can even wake me up when I’ve had just the right amount of sleep.
G: Interesting! I think AI could become something like our personal assistants.
B: I know, right? AI could help with our daily routines. Imagine what else it’ll do in the future. Is there anything you would like AI to be able to do for you?
G: An AI study aid would be really helpful. I would use it to help me with my French pronunciation.
B: Oh, I could also definitely use something like that for my foreign language class!
G: And think about it. After class, it could even suggest some cool things to do based on our interests or even our moods.
B: That sounds great! (A)I can’t wait to see what else AI can offer us in the future.

위 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: I’m excited to see
I’m thrilled to see
I’m curious to see
I’m reluctant to see
I’m looking forward to seeing
solution:
‘I can’t wait+to부정사‘는 ‘~하기를 무척 기대하다’라는 의미로, 어떤 일이나 경험에 대해 기대감과 설렘을 강하게 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현이다. ‘I’m curious to see ~’는 ‘~이 어떨지 궁금하다’라는 뜻이고, ‘I’m reluctant to see ~’는 ‘~을 보는 것이 꺼려진다’를 뜻하므로 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것은 ③ ‘~이 어떨지 궁금하다’, ④ ‘~을 보는 것이 꺼려진다’이다.
오답
① ~을 보는 것이 기대된다
② ~을 보게 되어 매우 기대된다
⑤ ~을 보는 것을 기대하고 있다

body:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been the subject of much discussion and controversy for many decades, with many experts (A)[predicting / predicted] that it will revolutionize our way of life. From healthcare to finance, the implementation of AI is transforming a wide range of sectors. (B)[Embrace / Embracing] AI means tapping into the potential of tomorrow in unprecedented ways. From self-driving cars to personalized medical treatments, AI is shaping our future and pushing the envelope like never before. As we stand on the brink of a new era, it is crucial that each of us (C)[understand / to understand] the rise of AI and its impacts on our world.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: predicting / Embrace / to understand
predicted / Embracing / understand
predicted / Embrace / understand
predicting / Embracing / to understand
predicting / Embracing / understand
solution:
(A) 전치사 with, 명사구 many experts와 함께 ‘with+명사(구)+현재분사/과거분사(~가 …하면서/한 채로)’의 부대상황을 나타내는 with분사구문을 이루고 있으며, many experts가 ‘예측하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 predicting이 알맞다.
(B) 뒤에 동사 means가 있으므로 주어 역할을 할 수 있는 동명사 Embracing이 알맞다.
(C) ‘중요성, 의무, 필요’ 등을 나타내는 형용사가 보어로 쓰인 ‘가주어(it) - 진주어(that절)’에서 that절 안의 동사는 주어의 인칭이나 시제에 관계없이 동사원형을 사용하며, ‘~해야 한다’는 의미의 조동사 should가 동사원형 앞에서 생략된다. 형용사 crucial(매우 중요한)은 ‘중요성’을 나타내므로 that절 안의 동사는 조동사 should가 생략된 동사원형 understand가 알맞다.

body:
AI is the ability of computers and machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as visual perception, speech recognition, decision-making, and language translation. Recent developments have also seen AI ______; AI art generators, for example, are able to take a human’s description in words and transform it directly into art. AI has been around for several decades, but recent advancements in computing power, data storage, and machine learning algorithms have fueled its rapid growth.
Some of the most significant impacts of AI are increased efficiency and productivity. Through automation, AI systems and robots can perform repetitive, boring, and dangerous tasks easily, freeing up humans to focus on more innovative and strategic work. In the healthcare sector, AI is being used to analyze vast amounts of medical data to improve diagnoses. In finance, AI algorithms are being used to automate administrative tasks, detect fraud, and make investment decisions.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: depending more heavily on human creativity to complete tasks
becoming less capable of producing original content
being limited to processing numbers and data
focusing only on simple and repetitive tasks
taking on more creative roles
solution:
also와 함께 쓰여 앞 문장에서 언급된 시각적 인식, 음성 인식, 의사 결정, 언어 번역과 같이 컴퓨터나 기계가 수행하는 영역에서, 기술의 발달로 어떤 것을 더 할 수 있는 AI를 목격할 수 있다는 흐름으로, 빈칸 뒤에 for example(예를 들면)과 함께 AI 미술 작품 생성기는 인간이 말로 묘사한 내용을 가지고 바로 미술 작품으로 변환할 수 있다는 구체적인 예시가 이어지므로, 이제 AI가 예술 작품을 만드는 창의적인 활동 또한 할 수 있다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘보다 창의적인 역할을 맡는 것’이 알맞다.

① 업무를 수행하기 위해 인간의 창의성에 더 크게 의존하는 것
② 독창적인 콘텐츠를 만들어 내는 능력이 점점 줄어드는 것
③ 숫자와 데이터를 처리하는 데만 제한되는 것
④ 단순하고 반복적인 업무에만 집중하는 것

solution:

body:
Advocates of AI argue ⓐwhat these advancements will lead to a more efficient, productive, and technical society, ⓑwhich individuals have more time and resources to focus on more meaningful work.
(A) Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries.
(B) This could lead to ⓒfinding solutions to climate change and cures for untreatable illnesses much quicker. Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment.
(C) They also argue that AI has the potential to solve complex problems, such as climate change and disease, in ways that ⓓwere previously impossible. For example, AI can analyze huge amounts of data quickly ⓔto find patterns in weather changes or the spread of a disease.
This ⓕcould lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: AI의 지지자들은 이러한 발전이 더 효율적이고 생산적인 사회를 만들어, 개인이 더 의미 있는 일에 집중할 시간과 자원을 늘릴 것이라고 주장한다는 주어진 글 뒤에, AI의 지지자들(Advocates of AI)을 They(그들)로 이어받아 also(또한)과 함께 AI가 기후 변화나 질병과 같은 복잡한 문제를 해결할 잠재력이 있다고 AI에 대한 긍정적 견해를 추가로 제시하는 (C), (C)의 마지막에서 AI가 날씨 변화나 질병 확산의 양상을 찾기 위해 많은 양의 데이터를 빠르게 분석할 수 있다고 언급한 뒤, 앞서 언급한 AI의 데이터 분석 능력을 This로 이어받아 이것이 기후 변화와 질병 문제의 해결로 이어질 수 있다고 설명하는 (B), (B)의 마지막에서 Meanwhile(한편)을 통해 AI에 대한 긍정적 견해에서 비판자들의 우려로 전환한 뒤, 앞서 제기된 AI의 고용에 대한 우려를 구체적으로, 자동화로 인해 기계와 로봇이 노동자를 대체하여 대규모 일자리 상실을 초래할 것이라고 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:

(C) They also argue that AI has the potential to solve complex problems, such as climate change and disease, in ways that ⓓwere previously impossible. For example, AI can analyze huge amounts of data quickly ⓔto find patterns in weather changes or the spread of a disease.
This ⓕcould lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓐ what → that (완전한 절(these ~ work)을 이끌어 동사 argue의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓑ which → where (콤마 뒤에서 완전한 절(individuals ~ work)을 이끌어, 콤마 앞의 명사구 a more efficient, productive, and technical society를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절이므로 관계부사 where로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ 구동사 ‘lead to(~으로 이어지다)‘의 to는 전치사이므로 lead to의 목적어 자리의 동명사 finding은 적절하다.
ⓓ 복수명사 ways를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절의 동사이며, 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 절의 동사는 선행사와 수일치하므로, 복수동사 were는 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(AI ~ quickly)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ’날씨 변화나 질병 확산의 양상을 찾기 위해‘라는 의미로 목적을 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to find는 적절하다.
ⓕ 과거 시제가 아니라 가능성을 나타내는 could이므로 적절하다.

solution:

This argument is not without merit. Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and ⓐit is likely that this trend will continue as AI becomes more widespread. ⓑ 완전한 절(automation ~ ones)을 이끌어 to consider의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.

body:
Some critics worry about ethical issues that are tied to AI, including its potential to maintain existing biases and discrimination. People often view computer systems as (A)[objective / subjective]. However, AI systems are only as unbiased as the data they are trained on; if that data contains biases, the AI system will likely (B)[eliminate / reproduce] those biases in its output.
For example, facial recognition algorithms have been found to be less accurate at recognizing individuals with certain types of skin tones. This is because the algorithms were trained on data sets that mostly contained faces with lighter skin tones. As a result, in the U.S., there have been incidents where people of racial minorities have been mistakenly identified as wanted criminals by facial recognition systems and wrongfully arrested by the police. This is a valid concern, and it is important for society to take steps to (C)[amplify / diminish] the potential negative impacts of AI.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: objective / reproduce / amplify
objective / eliminate / diminish
subjective / reproduce / amplify
subjective / eliminate / diminish
objective / reproduce / diminish
solution:
(A) 다음 문장이 However(그러나)로 연결되어 AI 시스템은 그것이 훈련된 데이터가 편향되지 않는 만큼만 편향되지 않을 수 있다고 했으므로, 사람들이 컴퓨터 시스템을 ‘객관적’이라고 여긴다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 objective(객관적인)가 적절하다.
subjective 주관적인
(B) 앞에서 AI 시스템은 그것이 훈련된 데이터가 편향되지 않는 만큼만 편향되지 않을 수 있다고 했으며, 뒤에 언급된 예시에서 안면 인식 알고리즘이 편향된 데이터로 인해 특정 피부색을 가진 사람의 인식 정확도가 떨어진다고 언급되었으므로, 데이터에 편향이 있다면 AI 시스템의 산출물에도 그러한 편향을 ‘재현할’ 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reproduce(재현하다)가 적절하다.
eliminate ~을 없애다
(C) AI 시스템이 기존의 편향과 차별을 지속 시킬 가능성에 대한 윤리적 우려에 대한 글로, 안면 인식 알고리즘이 편향된 데이터로 인해 소수 인종에 속하는 사람들이 부당하게 체포되는 사건이 있었던 것처럼, 사회는 AI의 이런 잠재적인 부정적 영향을 ‘줄일’ 대책을 취하는 것이 중요하다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 diminish(줄이다)가 적절하다.
amplify ~을 증폭시키다

body:
Merging with AI: We may be able to merge with AI in the future, enhancing our intelligence and life expectancy. What would it be like to be able to access the Internet with your mind? Then we might be able to think and learn at extraordinary speeds and control machines with our thoughts.
Bots taking the lead: Many traditional jobs might fade away, but exciting new roles may pop up. People might be trained to be mediators between AI and humans. Schools might teach teamwork among humans and bots rather than traditional subjects. Kids may attend “fusion schools” where AI instructor bots might collaborate with human creativity. Here, students can design artworks and invent games alongside their AI friends.
Scientific leaps: Artificial Superintelligence (ASI) can solve complex problems, allowing for phenomenal achievements in physics, medicine, climate science, and other fields at an unprecedented pace. For example, the spacecraft of the future may be capable of traveling to other planets at unimaginable speeds. They may also be equipped with advanced life support systems that will allow humans to live there for extended periods of time.
The technological singularity is a potentially dangerous event, but it is also one that could lead to incredible advances for humanity. We need to be aware of the risks and prepare for them as best we can, so that we can make sure that the singularity is a positive event for us all.

potential scientific discoveries resulting from advanced space exploration

This argument is not without merit.

Meanwhile, many critics of AI raise concerns about its impact on employment. Automation, they argue, will lead to widespread job losses, as machines and robots replace human workers in many industries. This could lead to increased poverty and income gap, as those who lose their jobs struggle to find new employment in an already competitive job market.
(A) Automation has already displaced workers in several industries, and it is likely that this trend will continue as AI becomes more widespread. (B) However, it is also important to consider that automation has been a driving force behind economic growth for centuries and has consistently created new job opportunities, even as it has decreased existing ones.
(C) For example, the rise of the automobile industry in the early 20th century led to the displacement of carriage drivers, but it also created new jobs in manufacturing, sales, and service. (D) The same can be said for the rise of the computer industry in the late 20th century, which displaced workers in manual labor industries, but also created new jobs in software development, information technology, and related fields. (E)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이 주장에는 타당한 점이 없지 않다.’라는 뜻으로, 이 문장 앞에는 This argument(이 주장)가 가리키는 특정한 주장이 제시되어야 하고, ‘타당한 점이 없지 않다’라고 했으므로 이 문장 뒤에는 왜 ‘이 주장’에 타당한 점이 있는지를 뒷받침하는 근거나 실제 사례가 제시되어야 한다. (A) 앞에서는 자동화로 인해 기계와 로봇이 인간 노동자를 대체하여 광범위한 실업을 초래하고, 이것이 빈곤과 소득 격차의 증가로 이어질 수 있다는 주장이 제시되었고, (A) 뒤에서는 실제로 여러 산업에서 자동화가 노동자를 대체해 왔으며 이러한 경향이 계속될 가능성이 있다고 설명하고 있다. (A) 뒤의 내용이 앞서 제기된 주장이 타당함을 뒷받침하는 근거로 이어지므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (A)이다.

body:
W: Every day, the world throws away billions and billions of plastic bottles. That's a problem. Of course, the real solution is to use less plastic. But it's cool that, even while we work to reduce plastic, some companies are turning trash into stuff we actually like. Drink it. Drop it in the bin. Take it to a recycling factory. Chop it up. Weave it. Wear it. Wash it. Wear it again. Wash it again. Seems like a great solution, right? But there's also a little problem that contributes to one big mess. Every time we wash synthetic fabrics, whether they are made from recycled bottles or brand-new materials, super tiny pieces of plastic, called microfibers, wash off and flow down the drain, up to hundreds of thousands each wash. The older our clothes get, the worse the problem can become! Yikes! These fibers are so tiny that water treatment plants don't catch them all. So they end up in rivers, lakes, and even the ocean.
위 담화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Although turning trash into useful products is helpful, the real solution is to use less plastic.
We as individuals are actively turning plastic bottles into new things to solve the plastic problem.
Brand-new clothes wash off more microfibers in the wash than old clothes.
Making clothes from recycled bottles involves many steps, such as chopping, weaving, and washing.
Water treatment plants cannot catch all of the tiny plastic fibers from our laundry.
solution:
쓰레기를 우리가 좋아할 만한 물건으로 바꾸고 있는 것은 기업들이라고 했으므로 ② ‘우리 개인들은 플라스틱 문제를 해결하기 위해 플라스틱병을 새로운 물건으로 적극적으로 바꾸고 있다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
옷이 오래될수록 미세섬유가 씻겨 나와 하수구로 흘러가는 문제가 더 심각해진다고 했으므로 ③ ’새 옷은 세탁할 때 오래된 옷보다 더 많은 미세섬유를 씻어 내보낸다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 쓰레기를 유용한 제품으로 바꾸는 것이 도움이 되기는 하지만, 진정한 해결책은 플라스틱을 덜 사용하는 것이다.
④ 재활용된 병으로 옷을 만드는 것은 자르고, 짜고, 씻는 것과 같은 많은 단계를 포함한다.
⑤ 정수 처리 시설은 우리의 세탁물에서 나온 아주 작은 플라스틱 섬유를 모두 걸러낼 수 없다.

We live surrounded by cloth. (A) We are covered with it at birth, we are made to wear clothes throughout our lives, and shrouds are drawn over our faces in death. (B) Wearing clothes is a specifically human characteristic, and most human societies use some form of clothing. (C) Textiles ─ artificial and natural ─ have shaped and changed the world we live in. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 인간의 삶과 문명에서 직물이 지닌 중요성과 직물의 역사에 대해 설명하는 글로, 직물은 인간의 삶과 함께해 왔으며, 인간 문명의 발전에도 영향을 미쳤으며, 따라서 직물의 역사를 살펴보는 것은 인간 문명의 발전을 이해하는 데 도움이 된다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용이다. body:
What to Wear for Space Travel
On July 21, 1969, 528 million people tuned in to watch the first human impression on the surface of the moon. Apollo 11 was the first space mission to take humans to the moon. One of the greatest challenges for this achievement involved manufacturing a space suit that could protect the astronauts: it would need to provide the astronauts with adequate air pressure and be able to withstand extreme temperatures ─ a maximum of 150°C in direct sunlight and a minimum of -233°C. However, such a technology did not exist in 1969.
Eight companies presented their solutions to NASA. ⓐ모두가 놀랍게도, 아폴로 우주복 계약을 따낸 업체는 다른 업체만큼 크지도 않은 데다 여성 속옷 제품군 덕분에 명성을 얻은 업체였다. The company came up with a softer and more flexible space suit made almost entirely of fabric. Each suit was made by seamstresses using their hands and sewing machines. Their skills were acquired from years of making women’s underwear. What made the work so hard was the number of layers and components involved. In the end, each suit worn on the moon was comprised of some four thousand pieces of fabric and twenty-one layers of distinct materials, weighing 72 kg at the time. It remains the most complex space suit to have been used to date, and it was the fruit of the craftsmanship of the women skilled in sewing and making underwear, rather than NASA’s technological expertise.
윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) A space suit to withstand extreme conditions was needed for the first moon mission. (T/F)
(B) NASA received proposals from eight companies, and the winning company had some experience in making space suits. (T/F)
(C) The company developed a space suit that was mostly made of fabric and offered greater softness and flexibility. (T/F)
(D) The workers who made the space suits had gained useful sewing skills through years of making women’s underwear. (T/F)
(E) Because the suits had a small number of layers and parts, they were relatively light. (T/F)
choices: F-T-T-T-F
T-F-T-F-F
T-T-F-F-T
T-F-T-T-F
T-F-T-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-T-F이다.

(E) 우주복은 층과 부품의 수가 적었기(→많았기) 때문에 비교적 가벼웠다(→무거웠다). (불일치)

During the 2008 Beijing Olympics, 25 new swimming world records were ⓐset. At the competition, a new type of swimsuit was worn by many swimmers. It was a full body swimsuit ⓑdesigned with a material that imitated shark skin. The suit allowed for better oxygen flow to the muscles, reduced water resistance, and added buoyancy by trapping air. In fact, some swimmers wore two or more of these suits at once to (A)[increase / reduce] buoyancy. In total, about 23 out of the 25 world records at the Beijing Olympics were set by swimmers ⓒwear this type of suit.
In later competitions, swimmers wearing various types of innovative swimsuits continued to break world records. As a result, in 2009, FINA, the international governing body for water sports, decided to (B)[prohibit / permit] all full body swimsuits. They also dictated ⓓthat the fabric used to make the suits must be breathable.
“Technology doping” in sports means the practice of gaining a competitive edge by using technology to improve performance. This can be against the spirit of fair play. However, since most sports require equipment of some sort, it can be (C)[easy / difficult] to determine what is technology doping and what is not. Some argue that it is a natural progress ⓔcoming from scientific development, while others claim it undermines human spirit and effort, ⓕensure that rich athletes have an advantage over poor ones.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓒ wear → wearing (명사 swimmers를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, swimmers가 ‘착용하는’ 주체이므로 wear를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 wearing으로 고친다.)
ⓕ ensure → ensuring (콤마(,) 앞의 완전한 절(it ~ effort)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사 구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 앞 절(it ~ effort)이 ‘확실하게 하는’ 주체이므로 ensure를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 ensuring으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 주어 25 new swimming world records가 ‘수립된“ 대상이므로, 앞의 be동사 were와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 set는 적절하다.
ⓑ 명사구 a full body swimsuit를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a full body swimsuit가 ’설계된‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 designed는 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(the fabric ~ breathable)을 이끌어 동사 dictated의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓔ 명사구 a natural progress를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a natural progress가 과학 발전으로부터 ’기인한‘ 주체이자 자동사 come이 쓰여 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 coming은 적절하다.
